ACCT 351.Title: Intermediate Financial Accounting 1
ACCT 351.Course_Description: An examination of the theoretical foundation for financial reporting and revenue recognition. The tools of accounting, including a review of the accounting process and compound interest concepts. Asset recognition, measurement and disclosure. Partnership accounting

ACCT 352.Title: Intermediate Financial Accounting 2
ACCT 352.Course_Description: A continuation of Intermediate Financial Accounting 1. An examination of liability recognition, measurement and disclosure, including leases, pension costs and corporate income tax. Shareholders' equity, dilutive securities and earnings per share. The statement of changes in financial position, basic financial statement analysis and full disclosure in financial reporting

ACCT 354.Title: Financial Statement Analysis
ACCT 354.Course_Description: Interpretative nature of the conceptual framework underlying a multitude of financial reporting standards, including the impact of alternative accounting methods, management biases and stakeholder interests in the analysis and valuation of the firm

ACCT 361.Title: Management Accounting
ACCT 361.Course_Description: The role of management accounting information to support internal management decisions and to provide performance incentives

ACCT 362.Title: Cost Accounting
ACCT 362.Course_Description: An examination of a number of recurring issues in the area of decision-making and control, including cost allocation, alternative costing systems, and innovations in costing and performance measurement

ACCT 385.Title: Principles of Taxation
ACCT 385.Course_Description: An introduction to the concepts underlying the Canadian tax system and how they are applied in relation to the taxation of individuals and businesses

ACCT 401.Title: Sustainability and Environmental Accounting
ACCT 401.Course_Description: Developing measures of corporate environmental performance, assessing their reliability and reporting to external stakeholders. Using sustainability metrics in strategic and operational business decisions. Implementing and utilizing Environmental management systems and standards. Managing corporate environmental risks and accounting for environmental costs. Environmental auditing

ACCT 434.Title: Topics in Accounting 1
ACCT 434.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 434.Course_Description: Topics will be selected from current issues in the Accounting Area

ACCT 451.Title: Data Analytics in Capital Market
ACCT 451.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 451.Course_Description: Exploration of how financial and non-financial metrics can be linked to business performance through experiential learning, with a focus on financial statement analysis, earnings and return predictability, textural analysis, earnings management and fraud detection. Introduction to SAS software and financial accounting databases such as CRSP, Compustat, and I/B/E/S, and alternative data sources such as SEC Edgar that enables work across different database to make better financial statement analysis and decisions

ACCT 452.Title: Financial Reporting Valuation
ACCT 452.Course_Description: Models to determine firm value from accounting information and a broader perspective on key sources of information, key value drivers, in a setting where evaluating firm value is the ultimate purpose

ACCT 453.Title: Advanced Financial Accounting
ACCT 453.Course_Description: Reporting relevant financial information subsequent to long term intercorporate investments. The preparation of consolidated financial statements with emphasis on their economic substance rather than legal form

ACCT 455.Title: Development of Accounting Thought
ACCT 455.Course_Description: The conceptual underpinning of accounting thought, including its historical development and the modifications that have occurred over time. A review of accounting literature and its relevance to practice

ACCT 463.Title: Management Control
ACCT 463.Course_Description: The theoretical frameworks for the examination and evaluation of management accounting and control systems. The technical aspects of accounting along with behavioural issues of management control

ACCT 475.Title: Principles of Auditing
ACCT 475.Course_Description: An introduction to basic auditing concepts and internal controls of an accounting system. Topics include current auditing standards, ethical conduct, legal liability, planning of an audit, sampling techniques, non-audit engagements, the study and evaluation of internal controls in an accounting system

ACCT 486.Title: Business Taxation 2
ACCT 486.Course_Description: A study of the Income Tax Act as it applies to the taxation of individuals and corporations, including capital cost allowances, capital gains, corporate reorganisations, trusts and partnerships and administrative regulations. A review of consumption taxes

ACCT 604.Title: Financial Statements 1
ACCT 604.Course_Description: Explores financial reporting and statement analysis, focusing on extracting and interpreting financial and non-financial information to assess and forecast firm performance. Covers accounting principles, major financial statements, ESG metrics, management biases, fraud detection, major financial patterns, and valuation. Evaluation of firm performance and application of valuation techniques

ACCT 605.Title: Financial Statements 2
ACCT 605.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 605.Course_Description: The company valuation process. Establish frameworks using public data

ACCT 618.Title: Financial Reporting: Structure and Analysis
ACCT 618.Course_Description: An in-depth analysis of corporate financial reporting principles and practices, with emphasis on developing the abilities of the student to discriminate between the form and substance of corporate financial reports. Analysis of all components of the financial statements with the effect of reference to alternative practices on financial reports

ACCT 623.Title: Intermediate Financial Reporting 2
ACCT 623.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 623.Course_Description: Theoretical foundation for financial reporting concepts such as liability and equity measurement, intercorporate investments

ACCT 626.Title: Data Analytics in Accounting
ACCT 626.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): (INSY 660 OR INSY 662 OR Instructor's approval) AND (MGSC 660 OR MGSC 661 OR Instructor's approval)
ACCT 626.Course_Description: Exploration of how financial and non-financial metrics can be linked to business performance through practica application learning. Examination of mandatory and voluntary corporate disclosure, financial statement analysis, return predictability, and fraud detection

ACCT 645.Title: Financial Management in Healthcare
ACCT 645.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 645.Course_Description: Concepts of financial accounting to the non-accountant user of financial information. Fundamental knowledge of financial accounting, including financial statements, accounting “rules”, assets, liabilities and equity, the income statements as well as the financial statement analysis

ACCT 645D1.Title: Financial Management in Healthcare
ACCT 645D1.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 645D1.Course_Description: Concepts of financial accounting to the non-accountant user of financial information. Fundamental knowledge of financial accounting, including financial statements, accounting “rules”, assets, liabilities and equity, the income statements as well as the financial statement analysis

ACCT 653.Title: Issues in Professional Accounting 1
ACCT 653.Course_Description: How fundamental concepts in financial accounting and reporting, including technically complex accounting issues and their audit, performance management, tax and finance implications, are integrated into decision-making

ACCT 654.Title: Issues in Professional Accounting 2
ACCT 654.Course_Description: Fundamental concepts in financial accounting and reporting, including technically complex accounting issues and their audit, performance management, tax and finance implications, are integrated into decision-making and strategies through case scenarios

ACCT 663.Title: Strategic Aspects of Accounting 1
ACCT 663.Course_Description: Corporate governance, strategy, risk management, and management reporting needs, with a particular emphasis on their integration with accounting practice, finance and taxation. Formulating deliberate and emergent strategies, and translating those strategies into specific objectives and actions which are used in decision-making

ACCT 664.Title: Strategic Aspects of Accounting 2
ACCT 664.Course_Description: Corporate governance, strategy, risk management, and management reporting needs, with a particular emphasis on their integration with accounting practice, finance and taxation. Emphasis is also placed on competence required to build good monitoring and control systems and perform financial analysis for different types of entities. Case scenarios are used to integrate these concepts into decision-making

ACCT 683.Title: Practice of Taxation
ACCT 683.Course_Description: Providing taxation services and guidance, including assisting individual and corporate entities to minimize taxes and meet their objectives while complying with tax laws and regulations. Addressing compliance and tax-planning issues for both individuals and corporate entities, as well as, to a lesser extent, partnerships and trusts. Recognizing the interrelationship between financial reporting decisions and taxation, and the importance of taking taxes into account when making business and investment decisions

ACCT 687.Title: Assurance Services
ACCT 687.Course_Description: Performing both internal audit projects and external assurance engagements; from understanding how governance plays a key role, assessing the need for an engagement, to developing and performing the procedures, through to documenting and reporting results

ACCT 689.Title: Financial Business Analysis
ACCT 689.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 689.Course_Description: Developing overall finance policies and identifying, analyzing, evaluating, and recommending investment and financing decisions. Applying appropriate finance principles and conceptual approaches to determine appropriate courses of action. Providing finance-related services for an entity, either individually or as part of a larger team, understanding when the advice of a finance specialist is required, and understanding and communicating with other finance professionals

ACCT 690.Title: Advanced Topics in Accounting 1
ACCT 690.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 690.Course_Description: A learning cell in which one or more students work with a faculty member

ACCT 695.Title: Integrative Analysis
ACCT 695.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): Any two of the following: ACCT 683, ACCT 685, ACCT 687, ACCT 689
ACCT 695.Course_Description: Integration of the enabling competencies and the six technical competency areas required of a CPA. Developing strategic leadership capabilities and the ability to bring an integrative perspective to decision-making including: professional and ethical behaviour, problem-solving and decision-making, communication (both written and oral), self-management, teamwork and leadership

ACCT 696.Title: Advanced Topics in Accounting Analytics
ACCT 696.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 696.Prerequisites: (INSY 660 OR INSY 662 OR Instructor's approval) AND (MGSC 660 OR MGSC 661 OR Instructor's approval)
ACCT 696.Course_Description: Current emerging topics in accounting analytics. Course content will vary each term

ACCT 699.Title: Exam Preparation Seminar
ACCT 699.Prerequisites: Any two courses of the following: ACCT 683, ACCT 685, ACCT 687, ACCT 689
ACCT 699.Course_Description: Using complex and highly integrative cases that simulate real-life business issues to apply the technical and enabling competencies acquired throughout the CPA certification program. Practicing developing responses to business simulations and communicating a well-structured response

ACCT 705.Title: Seminar in Accounting 1
ACCT 705.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.

ACCT 706.Title: Research Design in Accounting
ACCT 706.Course_Description: Course is designed in two parts. The first part covers major research design issues relevant to all fields of accounting. The second part addresses critical methodological issues specific to various fields of accounting research

ACCT 707.Title: Accountability and Sustainability
ACCT 707.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ACCT 707.Course_Description: The course provides an overview of key research on the broader role of accounting and accountability in shaping sustainable organizational and societal practices. The course focuses on most recent theoretical and empirical advances in two rapidly growing interrelated fields of research: environmental accounting and social accounting

AEBI 120.Title: Integrated Life Sciences
AEBI 120.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 120.Course_Description: Integrated survey of life sciences with emphasis on the interconnectivity of biological processes from the molecular to the ecosystem level. Analysis of energy flux, information transfer, and population dynamics within agricultural and environmental contexts

AEBI 210.Title: Organisms 1
AEBI 210.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 210.Course_Description: The biology of plants and plant-based systems in managed and natural terrestrial environments. The interactions between autotrophs and soil organisms and selected groups of animals with close ecological and evolutionary connections with plants (e.g., herbivores and pollinators) will be explored in lecture and laboratory

AEBI 211.Title: Organisms 2
AEBI 211.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 211.Course_Description: Introduction to the biology of heterotrophs, focusing on animal diversity from the perspectives of phylogenetics, physiology, and ecology. Introduction to major animal taxa, comparing and contrasting these taxa, and exploration of the relationships among them

AEBI 212.Title: Evolution and Phylogeny
AEBI 212.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 212.Course_Description: Overview of the tree of life and exploration of the central role evolution plays in the field of biology. Difficulties inherent to classifying life and critically assessing evolutionary theory among scientific and popular audiences. The importance of phylogenetics and the relationships among major groups of organisms

AEBI 421.Title: Tropical Horticultural Ecology
AEBI 421.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 421.Course_Description: A comprehensive survey of the major fruit, vegetable, turf, and ornamental crops grown in Barbados. Effect of cultural practices, environment, pests and pathogens, social and touristic activities, and importation of horticultural produce on local horticulture

AEBI 423.Title: Sustainable Land Use
AEBI 423.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 423.Course_Description: Management, preservation, and utilization of forage crops in sustainable tropical environments; examination of their value as livestock feed in terms of nutritional composition and impact on animal performance; land use issues as it pertains to forage and animal production in insular environments

AEBI 425.Title: Tropical Energy and Food
AEBI 425.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 425.Course_Description: Tropical biofuel crops, conversion processes and final products, particularly energy and greenhouse gas balances and bionutraceuticals. Topics include effects of process extraction during refining on biofuel economics, the food versus fuel debate and impact of biofuels and bioproducts on tropical agricultural economics

AEBI 427.Title: Barbados Interdisciplinary Project
AEBI 427.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEBI 427.Course_Description: The planning of projects and research activities related to tropical food, nutrition, or energy at the local, regional, or national scale in Barbados. Projects and activities designed in consultation with university instructors, government, NGO, or private partners, and prepared by teams of 2-3 students working cooperatively with these mentors

AEBI 665.Title: Fundamentals in Advanced Bioimaging
AEBI 665.Course_Description: Introduction to the principles of fluorescence microscopy, hands-on training on fluorescence imaging, a review of advanced fluorescence microscopy techniques with an emphasis on super-resolution microscopy, and case studies on the application of imaging techniques in biomedical research with a focus on infectious disease models

AECH 110.Title: General Chemistry 1
AECH 110.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AECH 110.Course_Description: The course will be a study of the fundamental principles of atomic structure, valence theory and the periodic table

AECH 111.Title: General Chemistry 2
AECH 111.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AECH 111.Course_Description: Thermodynamics, kinetics, equilibrium, aqueous solution chemistry including applications to acids, bases and buffers and selected topics in organic chemistry

AECH 118.Title: General Chemistry Laboratory 1
AECH 118.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AECH 118.Course_Description: The laboratory component of AECH 110 . Illustrative experiments

AECH 119.Title: General Chemistry Laboratory 2
AECH 119.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AECH 119.Course_Description: The laboratory component of AECH 111 . Illustrative experiments

AEHM 205.Title: Science Literacy
AEHM 205.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEHM 205.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AEHM 205.Course_Description: Development of English language and information literacy. Problem-based approach using science topics from specializations offered by the Faculty will be central to skill development. The course includes how to research and compose work in scientific format and will encourage a reader-oriented style

AEIS 230.Title: Indigenous Health and Nutrition
AEIS 230.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEIS 230.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AEIS 230.Course_Description: Examination of the histories impacting the contemporary nutrition, environment, and health of the Indigenous Peoples of Turtle Island by integrating Western and Indigenous knowledge systems with best practices in supporting Indigenous decision-making. Topics include: Indigenous knowledge systems and methodologies, Treaties and Reconciliation, Residential and Day schools, food sovereignty, environmental contamination and climate change, community-based participatory research, Indigenous access to health care, reflexivity and cultural safety, media advocacy strategies

AEMA 100.Title: Calculus for Life Sciences
AEMA 100.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 100.Course_Description: Fundamental concepts of calculus through a systems-based approach relevant to the life sciences. Limits, derivatives, integrals, and infinite series in biological contexts. Applications to population dynamics, pharmacology, physiological modelling, and quantitative agricultural and environmental systems

AEMA 101.Title: Calculus 1
AEMA 101.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 101.Course_Description: Review of functions and graphs. Limits, continuity, derivative. Differentiation of elementary functions. Antidifferentiation. Applications

AEMA 102.Title: Calculus 2
AEMA 102.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 102.Course_Description: Integration, the indefinite and definite integral. Trapezoidal and Simpson's Rule approximations for the integral. Applications to areas between curves, distance, volume, length of a curve, work, area of a surface of revolution, average values, moments, etc. Improper integrals and infinite series

AEMA 105.Title: Precalculus Lab
AEMA 105.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 105.Course_Description: Problem-solving: foundational material in algebra concepts, functions and graphs, polynomials and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, graphs and equations, trigonometry, analytic trigonometry, systems of linear equations, sequences & series

AEMA 202.Title: Intermediate Calculus
AEMA 202.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 202.Prerequisites: BREE 103 and AEMA 102 or equivalent CEGEP objectives 00UP and 00UQ or permission of instructor
AEMA 202.Course_Description: Methods of differential and integral calculus forthe study of multivariable functions. Calculus of parametric and polar curves, vectors and geometry of space, vector functions, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and their applications

AEMA 204.Title: Data Analytics for Biosystems
AEMA 204.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 204.Course_Description: Techniques and tools used to analyze agricultural and environmental data using some common programs (Microsoft Excel, Python, R, Jupyter Notebook, RStudio)

AEMA 305.Title: Differential Equations
AEMA 305.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 305.Course_Description: First and second order differential equations, Laplace transforms, numerical solutions, systems of differential equations, series solutions, applications to biological, chemical and engineering systems, use of computer-based mathematical tools

AEMA 310.Title: Statistical Methods 1
AEMA 310.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 310.Course_Description: Measures of central tendency and dispersion; binomial and Poisson distributions; normal, chi-square, Student's t and Fisher-Snedecor F distributions; estimation and hypothesis testing; simple linear regression and correlation; analysis of variance for simple experimental designs

AEMA 403.Title: Environmetrics Stage
AEMA 403.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 403.Prerequisites: Permission of the instructor based on satisfactory completion of the U2 year of the Environmetrics Domain in the McGill School of Environment
AEMA 403.Course_Description: Summer stage of at least four weeks, including a report. Provides students with professional experience in statistical analyses of environmental data. Can be undertaken at federal or provincial research stations and university research laboratories

AEMA 411.Title: Experimental Designs 01
AEMA 411.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 411.Course_Description: General principles of experimental design, split-plot designs, spatial heterogeneity and experimental design, incomplete block designs and unbalanced designs, analysis of repeated measures, multivariate and modified univariate analyses of variance, central composite designs

AEMA 414.Title: Temporal and Spatial Statistics 01
AEMA 414.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEMA 414.Course_Description: Temporal statistics: analysis in the time domain, Box-Jenkins forecasting methodology, analysis in the frequency domain, periodogram analysis. Spatial statistics: mapping, autocorrelogram analysis, geostatistics. Statistical inference with autocorrelated sample data

AEMA 610.Title: Statistical Methods 2
AEMA 610.Course_Description: Principles of linear models, multiple regression equations and classification models. Introduction to Analysis of Variance and common statistical designs used in agricultural and environmental sciences. Emphasis on balanced and unbalanced designs and data structures; their analysis and tests of statistical significance

AEMA 611.Title: Experimental Designs 1
AEMA 611.Course_Description: General principles of experimental design, split-plot designs, spatial heterogeneity and experimental design, incomplete block designs and unbalanced designs, analysis of repeated measures, multivariate and modified univariate analyses of variance, central composite designs

AEMA 614.Title: Temporal and Spatial Statistics 1
AEMA 614.Course_Description: Temporal statistics: analysis in the time domain, Box-Jenkins forecasting methodology, analysis in the frequency domain, periodogram analysis. Spatial statistics: mapping, autocorrelogram analysis, geostatistics. Statistical inference with autocorrelated sample data

AEPH 100.Title: Elements of Physics
AEPH 100.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 100.Course_Description: A conceptual survey of topics in physics relevant to the study of agricultural and environmental sciences: Newtonian mechanics, celestial motion, oscillations and waves, sound, electricity and magnetism, and light

AEPH 112.Title: Introductory Physics 1
AEPH 112.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 112.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AEPH 112.Course_Description: Kinematics in one and two dimensions. Newton's laws of motion. Circular motion and orbits. Rotation of a rigid body. Momentum. Work and energy, power. Conservation principles. Simple harmonic motion. Waves and sound

AEPH 113.Title: Physics 1
AEPH 113.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 113.Course_Description: Kinematics in one and two dimensions. Newton's laws of motion. Circular motion and orbits. Rotation of a rigid body. Momentum. Work and energy, power. Conservation principles. Simple harmonic motion. Waves and sound. Includes calculus-based applications

AEPH 114.Title: Introductory Physics 2
AEPH 114.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 114.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AEPH 114.Prerequisites: AEPH 112 or AEPH 113 or PHYS 101 or PHYS 131 or CEGEP objective 00UR or equivalents, or permission of instructor
AEPH 114.Corequisites: AEMA 102 (or MATH 141 or higher level calculus course) or CEGEP objective 00UP, or permission of instructor
AEPH 114.Course_Description: Electric and magnetic properties of matter: electrostatics, electric currents, the link between electric and magnetic phenomena, geometrical optics, interference diffraction

AEPH 115.Title: Physics 2
AEPH 115.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 115.Prerequisites: AEPH 112 or AEPH 113 or PHYS 101or PHYS 131 or equivalent
AEPH 115.Course_Description: Electric forces, electric fields, electric potential. Current. Electric circuits. Magnetic fields and forces. Electromagnetic induction. Electromagnetic waves. Geometrical and physical optics. Includes calculus-based applications

AEPH 120.Title: Physics Laboratory 1
AEPH 120.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 120.Course_Description: The laboratory component of AEPH 112 / AEPH 113 . Illustrative experiments

AEPH 122.Title: Physics Laboratory 2
AEPH 122.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AEPH 122.Course_Description: The laboratory component of AEPH 114 / AEPH 115 . Illustrative experiments

AERO 401.Title: Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
AERO 401.Faculty: Institute for Aerospace Eng. (Faculty of Engineering)
AERO 401.Course_Description: Basic concepts in all relevant aspects of aerospace engineering. Introduction to aircraft and spacecraft components, systems and operation. Aerodynamic and flight mechanics. Structures and materials. Propulsion systems. Manufacturing processes. Control and systems. Avionics and navigation

AERO 410.Title: Aerospace Design and Certification Process
AERO 410.Faculty: Institute for Aerospace Eng. (Faculty of Engineering)
AERO 410.Course_Description: Design and certification process for aircraft, helicopters and spacecraft. Operation and performance requirements. Preliminary and detailed design process. Performance analysis. Regulatory agencies overview. Certification process. Life cycle analysis. Cost analysis. Flight testing programs. Delivery and operation

AERO 460D1.Title: Aerospace Project
AERO 460D1.Faculty: Institute for Aerospace Eng. (Faculty of Engineering)
AERO 460D1.Course_Description: Application of the material learned in other courses in the Minor in Aerospace Engineering to an applied project. Team project work will involve the design, fabrication, verification, and application of an aerospace system / component. Lectures on topics related to design and management of design projects. Emphasis is on the completion of a project of professional quality in collaboration with the aerospace industry

AERO 460D2.Title: Aerospace Project
AERO 460D2.Faculty: Institute for Aerospace Eng. (Faculty of Engineering)

AERO 520.Title: Introduction to Aerospace Design
AERO 520.Faculty: Institute for Aerospace Eng. (Faculty of Engineering)
AERO 520.Course_Description: Multidisciplinary design of an aerospace vehicle thatconsiders the fluid mechanics, performance, stability andcontrol, avionics, electrical system, propulsion, structures,and materials in a systemapproach aimed for a set of specifications

AERO 633.Title: Aerodynamics
AERO 633.Course_Description: Equations of motion, vorticity and circulation, conformal mapping and flow round simple bodies. Two-dimensional flow around aerofoils. Flow separation. Flow around finite wings. High and low aspect-ratio wings. Propeller theory and design

AFRI 200.Title: Introduction to African Studies
AFRI 200.Course_Description: The African experience and current approaches to African studies, through adopting multidisciplinary perspectives on topics that include political conflict, governance and democratization, environment and conservation, economic development, rural life and urbanism, health and illness, gender, social change, popular culture, literature, film, and the arts

AFRI 401.Title: Swahili Language and Culture
AFRI 401.Course_Description: Basic knowledge of the Swahili language and culture with emphasis on handling circumstances that might be encountered in field research: everyday conversation, developing aural and oral skills and mastering basic grammar rules, understanding cultural norms and practices, issues of culture sensitivity and appropriateness

AFRI 480.Title: Honours Thesis
AFRI 480.Prerequisites: the completion of all available courses relevant to the topic, and permission of the instructor and Program Adviser prior to registration
AFRI 480.Course_Description: Supervised reading, research and preparation of an undergraduate thesis under the direction of a staff member

AFRI 481.Title: Special Topics 1
AFRI 481.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AFRI 481.Prerequisites: the completion of all available courses relevant to the topic, and permission of the instructor and Program Adviser prior to registration
AFRI 481.Course_Description: Supervised reading in advanced special topics in African Studies under the direction of a member of staff

AFRI 499.Title: Arts Internships: African Studies
AFRI 499.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AFRI 499.Course_Description: Internship with an approved host institution or organization

AFRI 598.Title: Research Seminar in African Studies
AFRI 598.Prerequisites: an introductory course in any of the disciplines studying Africa
AFRI 598.Course_Description: An interdisciplinary research seminar on topics of common interest to staff and students of the African Studies Program. As part of their contribution, students will prepare a research paper under the supervision of one or more members of staff

AFYR 101.Title: Complex Problems 1
AFYR 101.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AFYR 101.Course_Description: Introduction to an area of inquiry pertinent to multipledisciplines in Arts. Demonstrates how Arts disciplines address challenging problems or topics from distinct perspectives, employing different approaches and methodologies

AFYR 102.Title: Complex Problems 2
AFYR 102.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AFYR 102.Course_Description: An introduction to an area inquiry pertinent to multiple disciplines in Arts. Demonstrates how Arts disciplines address challenging problems or topics from distinct perspectives, employing different approaches and methodologies

AFYR 102AA.Title: The Fictions and Realities of Work
AFYR 102AA.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AFYR 102AA.Course_Description: Introduction to an area of inquiry pertinent to multipledisciplines in Arts. Demonstrates how Arts disciplines address challenging problems or topics from distinct perspectives, employing different approaches and methodologies

AGEC 200.Title: Principles of Microeconomics
AGEC 200.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 200.Course_Description: The field of economics as it relates to the activities of individual consumers, firms and organizations. Emphasis is on the application of economic principles and concepts to everyday decision making and to the analysis of current economic issues

AGEC 201.Title: Principles of Macroeconomics
AGEC 201.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 201.Course_Description: The overall economic system, how it works, and the instruments used to solve social problems. Emphasis will be on decision-making involving the entire economic system and segments of it

AGEC 231.Title: Economic Systems of Agriculture
AGEC 231.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 231.Course_Description: The structure and organization of Canada's agriculture-food system, the operation, financing, linkages, and functions of its components. Focus to be on management of the various components and the entire system, types of problems confronted now and in the future

AGEC 320.Title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
AGEC 320.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 320.Course_Description: An intermediate theory course in agricultural economics, dealing with economic concepts as applied to agricultural production and cost functions. Includes theory and application of linear programming as related to production decisions

AGEC 330.Title: Agriculture and Food Markets
AGEC 330.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 330.Course_Description: Nature and organization of agricultural and food markets as economic institutions, including the application of economic theory to problems within the agri-food marketing chain. Spatial and temporal price relationships, and the role of market structure

AGEC 332.Title: Farm Management and Finance
AGEC 332.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 332.Course_Description: Managing and financing a farm business. Topics include: the decision making process, farm management and economic concepts, the analysis of financial statements, farm planning and budgeting, input management, investment analysis, risk in financial management, the acquisition and cost of capital

AGEC 333.Title: Resource Economics
AGEC 333.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 333.Course_Description: The role of resources in the environment, use of resources, and management of economic resources within the firm or organization. Problem-solving, case studies involving private and public decision-making in organizations are utilized

AGEC 425.Title: Applied Econometrics
AGEC 425.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 425.Prerequisites: AEMA 310, AGEC 200 and AGEC 201 or equivalents
AGEC 425.Course_Description: The theory and application of econometrics to empirical issues in agriculture and environment. Diagnosis and treatment of standard violations of the assumptions underlying ordinary least squares

AGEC 430.Title: Agriculture, Food and Resource Policy
AGEC 430.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 430.Course_Description: Examination of North American and international agriculture, food and resource policies, policy instruments, programs and their implications. Economic analysis applied to the principles, procedures and objectives of various policy actions affecting agriculture, and the environment

AGEC 442.Title: Economics of International Agricultural Development
AGEC 442.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 442.Course_Description: The course deals with economic aspects of international development with emphasis on the role of food, agriculture and the resource sector in the economy of developing countries. Topics will include world food analysis, development project analysis and policies for sustainable development. Development case studies will be used

AGEC 450.Title: Agribusiness Management
AGEC 450.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 450.Prerequisites: AGEC 231, AGEC 330, AGEC 332 and an accounting course, or approval of instructor
AGEC 450.Course_Description: Strategic management of agricultural and food businesses. Analysis of internal and external factors and competitive forces affecting agribusinesses. Formulation of business strategy and solutions to strategic problems. Case-based course designed to enhance students' problemsolving and decisionmaking skills. Integration of knowledge and tools from various economics and business disciplines

AGEC 491.Title: Research and Methodology
AGEC 491.Faculty: Agricultural Economics (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGEC 491.Prerequisites: AGEC 201 or equivalent and AGEC 320 or permission of the instructor
AGEC 491.Corequisites: AGEC 425 or permission of the instructor
AGEC 491.Course_Description: Conceptual and philosophical foundations of research methodology, and the procedural aspects of planning, designing and conducting research in applied economics

AGEC 633.Title: Environmental and Natural Resource Economics
AGEC 633.Course_Description: An advanced course in the theory and problems of environmental and resource economics and in the analytical techniques used to assess environmental and resource use issues

AGEC 685.Title: Selected Topics in Agricultural Economics
AGEC 685.Course_Description: This course is designed to permit students to explore agricultural economics topics that are not covered in other courses. Students may be asked to prepare a presentation or lead discussion on the selected topic for the benefit of other students and staff. (Pass/Fail grading.)

AGEC 690.Title: Seminar in Agricultural Economics
AGEC 690.Course_Description: Current research on economic problems of agriculture, the agri-food system and the environment through presentations by staff, students and special guests. Article discussion on the latest issues and methods in agricultural economics

AGEC 692.Title: M.Sc. Thesis 2
AGEC 692.Course_Description: Literature review for the thesis research

AGEC 693.Title: M.Sc. Thesis 3
AGEC 693.Course_Description: Develop hypotheses for testing and identify the appropriate method

AGEC 694.Title: M.Sc. Thesis 4
AGEC 694.Course_Description: Research to be undertaken on hypotheses testing and interpreting results

AGEC 695.Title: M.Sc. Thesis 5
AGEC 695.Course_Description: Writing of the final version of the thesis under the supervision of the Supervisory Committee to be submitted for graduation

AGRI 120.Title: Exobiospheres
AGRI 120.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 120.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 120.Course_Description: Introduction to basic astronomical, biological, chemical and (geo)physical principles of systems capable of giving rise to and sustaining living structures, in both natural and artificial biospheres, within our solar system and beyond

AGRI 195.Title: Freshman Seminar 1
AGRI 195.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 195.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 195.Course_Description: Members of the Faculty and/or Student Services will present seminars on resources available to help students develop the requisite skills to facilitate their transition into university life

AGRI 196.Title: Freshman Seminar 2
AGRI 196.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 196.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 196.Course_Description: Members of the Faculty will present seminars on topical issues about their areas of research

AGRI 215.Title: Agro-Ecosystems Field Course
AGRI 215.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 215.Course_Description: Through case studies and field trips, students will examine the problems and constraints within the Canadian agro-ecosystem, including the interrelationships among food production, the environment, agricultural policy and social issues. Research in this field of study will also be introduced

AGRI 310.Title: Internship in Agriculture/Environment
AGRI 310.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 310.Course_Description: Internship on working farms or in other appropriate businesses of the agri-food/environment industries

AGRI 325.Title: Sustainable Agriculture Field Course
AGRI 325.Faculty: Animal Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 325.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 325.Prerequisites: AGEC 200 or equivalent; permission of the instructor
AGRI 325.Course_Description: Exposure to a foreign rural and agricultural context, to observe a variety of types of farm operations, cropping systems and techniques. The sustainability of these is discussed within their local social, environmental and economic landscapes

AGRI 330.Title: Agricultural Legislation
AGRI 330.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 330.Course_Description: A study of Quebec legislation of importance to the agricultural sector, with emphasis on the reasons why these laws were implemented and on their net effects on this sector. Some Canadian laws will be covered but only inasmuch as they affect Quebec agriculture

AGRI 340.Title: Principles of Ecological Agriculture
AGRI 340.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 340.Course_Description: Focus on low-input, sustainable, and organic agriculture: the farm as an ecosystem; complex system theory; practical examples of soil management, pest control, integrated crop and livestock production, and marketing systems

AGRI 401.Title: Honours Research Project 1
AGRI 401.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 401.Course_Description: Preparation of a literature review, progress report, and delivery of a proposal seminar, as well as initiating the research project

AGRI 402.Title: Honours Research Project 2
AGRI 402.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 402.Prerequisites: AGRI 401 and permission of the instructor
AGRI 402.Course_Description: Completion of the honours research project, including a progress report, a final project report, and a project presentation

AGRI 405.Title: Honours Project 1
AGRI 405.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 405.Course_Description: Preparation of a literature review, progress report and delivery of a proposal seminar, as well as initiating the research project

AGRI 406.Title: Honours Project 2
AGRI 406.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 406.Prerequisites: AGRI 405 and permission of the instructor
AGRI 406.Course_Description: Completion of the honours project, including a progress peport, a final project report, and a project presentation

AGRI 410.Title: Agrology Internship
AGRI 410.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 410.Course_Description: Professional internship (stage) under the supervision of a practicing agrologist

AGRI 410D1.Title: Agrology Internship
AGRI 410D1.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 410D1.Course_Description: Professional internship (stage) under the supervision of a practicing agrologist

AGRI 410D2.Title: Agrology Internship
AGRI 410D2.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)

AGRI 411.Title: Global Issues on Development, Food and Agriculture
AGRI 411.Faculty: Animal Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 411.Course_Description: International development and world food security and challenges in developing countries. Soil and water management, climate change, demographic issues, plant and animal resources conservation, bio-products and biofuels, economic and environmental issues specially in tropical and sub-tropical regions. Globalization, sustainable development, technology transfer and human resources needs for rural development

AGRI 430.Title: Professional Practice in Agrology
AGRI 430.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 430.Course_Description: This course introduces students to the professional aspects of the practice of agrology. Topics include understanding the responsibilities of agrologists, the broad context and functioning of the Québec agricultural industry, how to deal with clients, colleagues, and understanding legal and regulatory aspects of the profession in Québec

AGRI 435.Title: Soil and Water Quality Management
AGRI 435.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 435.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 435.Course_Description: Management of soil and water systems for sustainability. Cause of soil degradation, surface and groundwater contamination by agricultural chemicals and toxic pollutants. Human health and safety concerns. Water-table management. Soil and water conservation techniques will be examined with an emphasis on methods of prediction and best management practices

AGRI 452.Title: Water Resources in Barbados
AGRI 452.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 452.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 452.Course_Description: Physical environment challenges, centered on water, being faced by an island nation. Guest speakers, field study tours and laboratory tests. Private, government and NGO institutional context of conservation strategies, and water quantity and quality analyses for water management specific to Barbados

AGRI 490.Title: Agri-Food Industry Project
AGRI 490.Faculty: Plant Science (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 490.Course_Description: Interdisciplinary team project in the agri-food industry

AGRI 493.Title: International Project Management
AGRI 493.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 493.Course_Description: Principles and practice related to management of agriculture, nutrition and environmental projects within an international context. Case-studies and workshops drawing on expertise of development professionals from government and the private sector address techniques and resources for successful planning, implementation and evaluation within a multi-sectoral framework

AGRI 498.Title: Agricultural Development Research
AGRI 498.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 498.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 498.Course_Description: Supervised reading and research project related to agriculture, food systems, nutrition and health in developing countries

AGRI 499.Title: Agricultural Development Internship
AGRI 499.Faculty: Agricultural & Env.Sc.-Dean (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 499.Course_Description: Supervised internship to provide practical experience working on agricultural issues related to international development. The internship can take many forms, including work in a developing country, for an agency that focuses on international development, or on a research project that aims at solving problems faced by developing populations

AGRI 510.Title: Professional Practice
AGRI 510.Faculty: Food Science&Agr.Chemistry (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 510.Course_Description: The ethical issues that face a professional in the workplace; professional ethics and deontology, professional responsibilities as related to the laws of labour, health, safety and risks to the environment, risk management and communication

AGRI 519.Title: Sustainable Development Plans
AGRI 519.Faculty: Bioresource Engineering (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 519.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
AGRI 519.Course_Description: Geared for solving real-world environmental problems related to water at the local, regional and international scale in Barbados. Projects to be designed by instructors in consultation with university, government and NGO partners and to be conducted by teams of 2 to 4 students in collaboration with them

AGRI 550.Title: Sustained Tropical Agriculture
AGRI 550.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
AGRI 550.Prerequisites: HISP 218 or equivalent; MATH 203 or AEMA 310 or equivalent
AGRI 550.Course_Description: Contrast theory and practice in defining agricultural environmental "challenges" in the Neotropics. Indigenous and appropriate technological means of mitigation. Soil management and erosion, water scarcity, water over-abundance, and water quality. Explore agro-ecosystem protection via field trips and project designs. Institutional context of conservation strategies, NGO links, and public participation

ANAE 301.Title: TCP Anesthesia
ANAE 301.Course_Description: This two-week required course exposes students to Anesthesia through lectures, simulated activities and supervised participation in perioperative patient care. Learning experiences relate to the basics of resuscitation, pain management, and preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative anesthesia care. Students will demonstrate understanding of clinical applications of pharmacology and physiology

ANAE 401.Title: Anesthesia Clerkship
ANAE 401.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ANAE 401.Course_Description: Introduction to the principles and procedures of anesthesiology, including pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative anesthetic techniques. Practice procedures commonly performed by Anesthetists (bag and mask ventilation, endotracheal intubation, and intravenous insertion). The basics of resuscitation, peri-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative anesthesia care, including assessing and treating acute and chronic pain. Clinical applications of pharmacology and physiology underpinning anesthesiology

ANAT 212.Title: Molecular Mechanisms of Cell Function
ANAT 212.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 212.Course_Description: An introductory course describing the biochemistry and molecular biology of selected key functions of animal cells, including: gene expression; mitochondrial production of metabolic energy; cellular communication with the extra-cellular environment; and regulation of cell division

ANAT 214.Title: Systemic Human Anatomy
ANAT 214.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 214.Prerequisites: BIOL 112 (or CEGEP equivalent), PHGY 209 and PHGY 210
ANAT 214.Course_Description: Introduction to the gross anatomy of the various organ systems of head, neck and trunk regions of the human body. Emphasis on functional anatomy. Laboratory component includes exploration of the human body through cadaveric prosections, imaging and other materials

ANAT 261.Title: Introduction to Dynamic Histology
ANAT 261.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 261.Course_Description: An introduction to light and electron microscopic anatomy in which cell and tissue dynamics will be explored in the principal tissues and organs of the body

ANAT 262.Title: Introductory Molecular and Cell Biology
ANAT 262.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 262.Course_Description: The architectural, functional and temporal continuity of organelles and the cytoskeleton of mammalian cells is introduced as well as their functional integration in the phenomena of exocytosis, endocytosis, protein trafficking and cell motility and adhesion

ANAT 314.Title: Human Musculoskeletal Anatomy
ANAT 314.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 314.Course_Description: Introduction to the gross anatomy of the musculoskeletal system (bone, joints, muscles and neurovascular structures) of the head, neck, trunk, upper and lower limb regions of the human body, emphasizing functional anatomy and including surface anatomy and imaging. Exploration of the human body through cadaveric prosections, imaging and other materials

ANAT 315.Title: Clinical Human Musculoskeletal Anatomy
ANAT 315.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 315.Course_Description: The regional human gross anatomy of the skeleton, joints, muscles and neurovascular structures of the body as it relates to physical and occupational therapists. Laboratories include the study of prepared cadaveric specimens and the completion of a cadaveric-dissection

ANAT 316.Title: Clinical Human Visceral Anatomy
ANAT 316.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 316.Course_Description: The gross anatomy of the various organ systems of the human body, with emphasis on those aspects of greatest relevance to physical and occupational therapists. Laboratories include the study of prepared specimens

ANAT 321.Title: Circuitry of the Human Brain
ANAT 321.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 321.Prerequisites: ANAT/BIOC 212 or BIOL 201; and one of PHGY 209, NSCI 200 or PSYC 211; or permission of instructor
ANAT 321.Course_Description: This course explores the functional organization of the human brain and spinal cord. The course focuses on how neuronal systems are designed to subserve specific motor, sensory, and cognitive operations

ANAT 322.Title: Neuroendocrinology
ANAT 322.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 322.Course_Description: A lecture course describing brain-endocrine relationships. Emphasis on modern experimental evidence and conceptual developments within the field

ANAT 323.Title: Clinical Neuroanatomy
ANAT 323.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 323.Prerequisites: Prerequisites for Honours Anatomy & Cell Biology students: ANAT 214 and ANAT 314
ANAT 323.Course_Description: This course will focus on the structural and functional relationships of the central nervous system. The human neuroanatomy will be introduced via pathological cases and will be illustrated by use of new medical imaging techniques

ANAT 365.Title: Cellular Trafficking
ANAT 365.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 365.Prerequisites: ANAT 261, ANAT 262, PHGY 209, or by permission of instructor
ANAT 365.Course_Description: This course explores the fundamental mechanisms that govern the organizations of intracellular membranes, how vesicle generation is signaled, how the membranes curve and bud, and how vesicles know where to go and fuse. In addition to intracellular vesicles, the principles of mitochondrial dynamics and process of cellular autophagy are examined. Also, there is a focus on "Applied Cell Biology", with respect to how the exquisite regulation of cellular transport plays a central role in complex biological systems. A series of modules will take students through the mechanisms of cellular polarity, neurotransmission, metabolic cell biology, pathogen invasion, and more. The emphasis is on the morphological aspects of the processes, and on the major techniques that led to discovery

ANAT 381.Title: Experimental Embryology
ANAT 381.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 381.Prerequisites: ANAT 261, BIOL 202 or permission of instructor
ANAT 381.Course_Description: The basic processes of reproduction and embryonic development, such as molecular signaling; cell-cell interaction; differentiation; cell fate determination; genetic and epigenetic control of embryonic development

ANAT 396.Title: Undergraduate Research Project
ANAT 396.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 396.Course_Description: Independent research project with a final written report

ANAT 416.Title: Development, Disease and Regeneration
ANAT 416.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 416.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): ANAT 381 or BIOL 303 or special permission of instructor
ANAT 416.Course_Description: Importance of developmental biology for disease and regeneration. Topics: advanced developmental biology principles; molecular basis for stem cells and their potential applications; organogenesis and its applications to various diseases

ANAT 432.Title: Honours Research Project
ANAT 432.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 432.Course_Description: Supervised honours research project in biological sciences

ANAT 432D1.Title: Honours Research Project
ANAT 432D1.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 432D1.Course_Description: Supervised honours research project in biological sciences

ANAT 432D2.Title: Honours Research Project
ANAT 432D2.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)

ANAT 458.Title: Membranes and Cellular Signaling
ANAT 458.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 458.Prerequisites: BIOC 212 or ANAT 212 or BIOL 201, ANAT 262, one of PHGY 209 or BIOL 205; one of BIOC 312 or ANAT 365; BIOC 311 recommended
ANAT 458.Course_Description: An integrated treatment of the properties of biological membranes and of intracellular signaling, including the major role that membranes play in transducing and integrating cellular regulatory signals. Biological membrane organization and dynamics; membrane transport; membrane receptors and their associated effectors; mechanisms of regulation of cell growth, morphology, differentiation and death

ANAT 499.Title: Supervised Library Research
ANAT 499.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 499.Course_Description: Supervised exploration of the current scientific literature as it pertains to the advanced field of anatomy and cell biology

ANAT 514.Title: Advanced Human Anatomy Laboratory
ANAT 514.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 514.Course_Description: A laboratory course exploring human anatomy education through regionally focused dissection-based projects and applications of technology in anatomy teaching and learning

ANAT 541.Title: Cell and Molecular Biology of Aging
ANAT 541.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 541.Prerequisites: ANAT 212 (or BIOC 212 or BIOL 201), ANAT 261, ANAT 262, or permission of instructor
ANAT 541.Course_Description: Complex aging process, including theories and mechanisms of aging, animal model systems used to study aging, age-dependent diseases, for example, Alzheimer's, osteoporosis, and cancer, and age-related diseases, for example, Werner's syndrome and dyskeratosis congenita

ANAT 542.Title: Transmission Electron Microscopy of Biological Samples
ANAT 542.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 542.Course_Description: Overview of theory, principles and practical applications of conventional and cryo-transmission electron microscopy relevant to biological samples. Major topics to be covered include: sample preparation and imaging, image analysis, three-dimensional reconstruction (including single-particle analysis an tomography)

ANAT 565.Title: Diseases-Membrane Trafficking
ANAT 565.Faculty: Anatomy and Cell Biology (Faculty of Science)
ANAT 565.Course_Description: This course will examine how research into diseases has played a key role in unraveling the intricate molecular mechanisms controlling membrane trafficking in mammalian cells. Membrane trafficking disorders fall into two groups those arising from a) membrane-associated or b) cytoskeletal defect. Topics include a) mechanisms of endosomal maturation, lysosomal storage disorders and rab protein-mediated vesicular trafficking and b) rho GTPase and cytoskeletal binding protein mediated trafficking associated with neurological diseases and cancer

ANAT 601.Title: MSc Seminar Examination
ANAT 601.Course_Description: The term before the student graduates, the student is to present a 30 minute seminar on their thesis work in a public seminar open to all members of the Department of Anatomy & Cell Biology, followed by a question period lasting 15 to 20 minutes. All faculty, cross-appointed academic staff, post docs and students are expected to attend the seminar

ANAT 690D1.Title: Cell and Developmental Biology
ANAT 690D1.Course_Description: Current developments in molecular cell biology and developmental biology will be presented by course coordinators and staff from primary papers in the scientific literature. These will be researched and critiqued by students through oral and written presentations. Two term papers are required for students taking the course

ANAT 695.Title: Seminars in Cell Biology 1
ANAT 695.Course_Description: Weekly assignments based on seminars attended will be graded by the supervisor. A grade of P or F will be assigned

ANAT 696.Title: Seminars in Cell Biology 2
ANAT 696.Course_Description: Weekly assignments based on seminars attended will be graded by the supervisor. A grade of P or F will be assigned

ANAT 697.Title: Seminars in Cell Biology 3
ANAT 697.Course_Description: Weekly assignments based on seminars attended will be graded by the supervisor. A grade of P or F will be assigned

ANAT 698.Course_Description: Independent research work under the direction ofthe Thesis Supervisor and the guidance of the thesis advisory Committee

ANAT 698D1.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ANAT 698D1.Course_Description: Independent research work under the direction ofthe Thesis Supervisor and the guidance of the thesis advisory Committee

ANAT 698D2.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ANAT 698D2.Course_Description: Independent research work under the direction ofthe Thesis Supervisor and the guidance of the thesis advisory Committee

ANAT 701.Course_Description: Compulsory comprehensive examination to evaluate the students' ability to carry out, present, discuss and defend research in their field of scientific interest

ANAT 701D1.Course_Description: Compulsory comprehensive examination to evaluate the students' ability to carry out, present, discuss and defend research in their field of scientific interest
