NSCI 430D1.Title: Honours Research Project
NSCI 430D1.Course_Description: Students undertake an independent research project in the field of neursocience under the guidance of an established McGill neuroscientist. They are expected to obtain hands-on research experience in their supervisor's laboratory, learn about the strengths and limitations of the methodology and work independently

NSCI 430D2.Title: Honours Research Project
NSCI 430D2.Course_Description: Students undertake an independent research project in the field of neursocience under the guidance of an established McGill neuroscientist. They are expected to obtain hands-on research experience in their supervisor's laboratory, learn about the strengths and limitations of the methodology and work independently

NUTR 207.Title: Nutrition and Health
NUTR 207.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 207.Corequisites: FDSC 230 [for students that have not taken the CEGEP equivalent OOXV]
NUTR 207.Course_Description: Provides students who have a basic biology/chemistry background with the fundamental information on how macronutrients, vitamins and minerals are metabolized in the body, followed by application to evaluate current issues of maximizing health and disease prevention at different stages of the lifecycle

NUTR 208.Title: Professional Practice Stage 1A
NUTR 208.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 208.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): All U0 (freshman) science/math entrance requirements or permission of instructor
NUTR 208.Corequisites: Corequisite(s): All Required courses in Term 1 of the Dietetics Major, IPEA 500
NUTR 208.Course_Description: Introduction to the dietetics profession including ethics; provincial regulation; competencies and domains of practice; and dietetic practice in the hospital environment. Introductory activities related to food, food industry, agriculture, public health nutrition and clinical nutrition

NUTR 209.Title: Professional Practice Stage 1B
NUTR 209.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 209.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): All U0 math and science entrance requirements. All U1 required courses of the Dietetics major (ANSC 234, LSCI 211, LSCI 230, NUTR 207, NUTR 208, NUTR 214, NUTR 217, NUTR 322, NUTR 343 and NUTR 341)
NUTR 209.Course_Description: Introductory dietetic internship experience. Introduction to the hospital environment, client- centred care and the patient experience. Communication, dietary assessment, and nutrition education

NUTR 214.Title: Food Fundamentals
NUTR 214.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 214.Prerequisites: FDSC 230 or corequisite with instructor's permission
NUTR 214.Course_Description: Food composition and structure. Scientific principles underlying physical, chemical, and nutrient content changes during food preparation. The role of ingredients and nutrients, and their interaction in food preparation. Culture of food including historical context and sustainability. Sensory evaluation and food safety

NUTR 217.Title: Application: Food Fundamentals
NUTR 217.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 217.Course_Description: Nutrition, chemical and physical properties of food and complex food mixtures. Role of culture, food policy and environmental sustainability on food choices, procurement and preparation. Knowledge of ingredients, preservation, storage, packaging of food. Culturally diverse foods and food habits. Controlling chemical changes during preparation of food to obtain palatable, nutritious and safe food

NUTR 301.Title: Psychology
NUTR 301.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 301.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
NUTR 301.Course_Description: A study of the general characteristics of physical, social, emotional and intellectual development, the psychology of learning, and the growth and development of personality

NUTR 307.Title: Metabolism and Human Nutrition
NUTR 307.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 307.Course_Description: This course looks at the importance of nutrition from the molecular to the organismal levels in human health and disease. The focus will be on the significance of nutrients in regulating metabolism, and impact of genotype in the metabolism of nutrients

NUTR 310.Title: Professional Practice Stage 2A
NUTR 310.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 310.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): Fall term U2 required Dietetics Major courses
NUTR 310.Course_Description: The nutrition care process, clinical reasoning and documentation for the medical record. Preparation for the application of knowledge in practice, for clinical nutrition and food service administration rotations, will be addressed

NUTR 311.Title: Professional Practice Stage 2B
NUTR 311.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 311.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): All U2 required courses: AEMA 310, NUTR 343, ANSC 323, ANSC 424, NUTR 307, NUTR 310, NUTR 337 (NUTR 342 or NUTR 446), NUTR 344, NUTR 345, NUTR 346
NUTR 311.Course_Description: Two interrelated modules of directed experience in normal and clinical nutrition and food service management, in health care settings and the private sector

NUTR 322.Title: Applied Sciences Communication
NUTR 322.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 322.Prerequisites: Completion of 15 credits in a B.Sc. program
NUTR 322.Course_Description: The principles and techniques of communicating applied sciences to individuals and groups in both the professional and public milieu. Effective public speaking and group interaction techniques. Communication materials selection, development, use, and evaluation. Writing for the media. Balancing risk and reason in communicating scientific findings

NUTR 337.Title: Nutrition Through Life
NUTR 337.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 337.Course_Description: Nutrient utilization, requirements and recommended allowances as related to physiological development throughout the life cycle. Physiological, psychological and environmental determinants of eating behaviour

NUTR 341.Title: Global Food Security
NUTR 341.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 341.Corequisites: Corequisite(s): NUTR 207 or permission of Instructor
NUTR 341.Course_Description: Food insecurity is one of the most critical issues humanity has faced in history. The magnitude of this phenomenon, reflected in its worldwide presence and in the number of individuals affected, makes it an imperative component of all nations' and of all internaltional agencies' agendas. Its complexity of determinants and its numerous consequences require the involvement of multipe disciplines and sectors. McGill undergraduate students as future professionals tackling global issues require an integrated and multidisciplinary training on food security

NUTR 342.Title: Applied Human Resources
NUTR 342.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 342.Course_Description: This course provides a solid foundation of HR essentials and a philosophy from which to navigate in the work place, familiarity with federal and provincial legislation and knowledge of current challenges and issues; a discussion on the employee life cycle from recruitment and selection to termination and everything that happens in between; a paradigm for leadership and creating a culture of engagement and effectiveness

NUTR 343.Title: Financial Management and Accounting
NUTR 343.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 343.Course_Description: Priniciples and concepts of financial management, accounting and cost control, analysis, utilization and communication of financial information. Cost value profit analysis, budgets and decision-making with applications in the food and nutrition sector

NUTR 344.Title: Clinical Nutrition 1
NUTR 344.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 344.Course_Description: Clinical nutrition assessment and dietary modification of pathological conditions including hypertension, lipid disorders and cardiovascular disease, obesity, cancer, COPD, introduction to diabetes, dysphagia

NUTR 345.Title: Food Service Systems Management
NUTR 345.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 345.Course_Description: Competency-based professional course for management of food service systems in healthcare organizations, food service industry, and groups. Principles of management theory and development of business plan in nutritionrelated activities. Emphasis on strategic planning; food policies; menu development; recipe standardization, nutrient analysis, costing; food purchasing; quality control; marketing; staffing; management styles; and ethical and professional behaviour. Students receive Canadian Food Safety Certification (Advanced.fst) upon completion of this course

NUTR 346.Title: Applied Food Service Management
NUTR 346.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 346.Course_Description: Competency-based professional course focusing on human resources management, marketing, budgeting, HACCP principles, allergen management, recipe standardization, local and federal sanitation laws, and quality assurance in food settings and case studies. Students receive Allergen and WHMIS certification upon completion of this course

NUTR 401.Title: Emerging Issues in Nutrition
NUTR 401.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 401.Course_Description: Investigation, discussion and presentations of emerging issues in nutrition

NUTR 408.Title: Professional Practice Stage 3A
NUTR 408.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 408.Course_Description: Competency-based educational topics linking theory to practice for field placements in the clinical setting. Topics include ethics, leadership and interprofessional teamwork

NUTR 409.Title: Professional Practice Stage 3B
NUTR 409.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 409.Prerequisites: NUTR 311, NUTR 342 or NUTR 446 , NUTR 450, NUTR 505, NUTR 545 and NUTR 546
NUTR 409.Course_Description: Four interrelated modules of directed experience in clinical nutrition, food service management, normal nutrition education and community nutrition, in health care settings and the private sector

NUTR 430.Title: Directed Studies: Dietetics and Nutrition 1
NUTR 430.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 430.Course_Description: An individualized course of study in dietetics/human nutrition under the supervision of a staff member with expertise on a topic not otherwise available in a formal course. A written agreement between student and staff member must be made before registration and filed with the Program Coordinator

NUTR 431.Title: Directed Studies: Dietetics and Nutrition 2
NUTR 431.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 431.Course_Description: An individualized course of study in dietetics/human nutrition under the supervision of a staff member with expertise on a topic not otherwise available in a formal course. A written agreement between student and staff member must be made before registration and filed with the Program Coordinator

NUTR 431D1.Title: Directed Studies: Dietetics and Nutrition 2
NUTR 431D1.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 431D1.Course_Description: An individualized course of study in dietetics/human nutrition under the supervision of a staff member with expertise on a topic not otherwise available in a formal course. A written agreement between student and staff member must be made before registration and filed with the Program Coordinator

NUTR 431D2.Title: Directed Studies: Dietetics and Nutrition 2
NUTR 431D2.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)

NUTR 432.Title: Directed Studies: Dietetics and Nutrition 3
NUTR 432.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 432.Course_Description: An individualized course of study in dietetics/human nutrition under the supervision of a staff member with expertise on a topic not otherwise available in a formal course. A written agreement between student and staff member must be made before registration and filed with the Program Coordinator

NUTR 433.Title: Directed Studies: Dietetics and Nutrition 4
NUTR 433.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 433.Course_Description: An individualized course of study in dietetics and human nutrition not available through other courses in the School. Emphasis will be placed on application of foods and nutrition knowledge, analytic and synthesis skills, and time management. A written agreement between student and instructor must be made before registration. A "C" grade is required to pass the course

NUTR 438.Title: Interviewing and Counselling
NUTR 438.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 438.Course_Description: Theories of behaviour change. Techniques and skills as applicable to the dietitian's role as communicator, interviewer, counsellor, educator, motivator and nutrition behaviour change specialist

NUTR 450.Title: Research Methods: Human Nutrition
NUTR 450.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 450.Course_Description: Introduction to how diverse approaches to nutrition research including international, community, laboratory, clinical, molecular, meta-analyses are necessary to advance the field of nutrition. Emphasis on ethics, scientific method, research process and analysis of results

NUTR 480.Title: Nutrition Industry Internship
NUTR 480.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 480.Course_Description: Internship with an approved host organization in the nutrition product industry

NUTR 491.Title: Honours Research 1
NUTR 491.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 491.Course_Description: The first part of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member in the School of Human Nutrition. Development of research proposal, including literature review, objectives, and research plan. Presentation and submission of written proposal

NUTR 492.Title: Honours Research 2
NUTR 492.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 492.Prerequisites: NUTR 491 and permission of the instructor
NUTR 492.Course_Description: The second part of a research project that tests the hypothesis developed in the research proposal. Collection of data, initial interpretation of findings, progress report and plan

NUTR 493.Title: Honours Research 3
NUTR 493.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 493.Prerequisites: NUTR 492 and permission of the instructor
NUTR 493.Course_Description: The third part of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member in the School of Human Nutrition with completion of study, data analysis, and written progress report

NUTR 494.Title: Honours Research 4
NUTR 494.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 494.Prerequisites: NUTR 493 and permission of the instructor
NUTR 494.Course_Description: Completion of research project, with final interpretation of data in written manuscript-style report and defended in conference-style presentation

NUTR 497.Title: Professional Seminar: Nutrition
NUTR 497.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 497.Course_Description: A capstone course which requires a student to research a topic relevant to an industrial aspect of Nutritional Science, prepare a report and communicate that information to a peer audience in a succinct and professional manner

NUTR 500.Title: Independent Study 1
NUTR 500.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 500.Prerequisites: Permission of instructor and Director of the School
NUTR 500.Course_Description: An individualized course to allow students to undertake projects in library, laboratory, or field study

NUTR 501.Title: Nutrition in the Majority World
NUTR 501.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 501.Prerequisites: A course in nutrition across the lifespan at the intermediate undergraduate level such as NUTR 337, or permission of the instructor
NUTR 501.Course_Description: Current nutrition-related issues in the Majority World, emphasizing young children and other vulnerable groups. The integration of a life science and social science perspective. The multiple causes, consequences, policies, and interventions related to current nutrition

NUTR 502.Title: Independent Study 2
NUTR 502.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 502.Prerequisites: Permission of instructor and Director of the School
NUTR 502.Course_Description: An individualized course to allow students to undertake projects in library, laboratory, or field study

NUTR 503.Title: Nutrition and Exercise
NUTR 503.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 503.Prerequisites: Undergraduate Basic Biochemistry (ANSC 234 or BIOC 311), Undergraduate Mammalian Physiology (EDKP 395 or PHGY 210 or ANSC 323), Undergraduate Introductory Nutrition (EDKP 292 or NUTR 207 or NUTR 307)
NUTR 503.Course_Description: Interaction of exercise physiology with nutrient and energy metabolism in healthy adults. Principles of physical training and role of physical activity and exercise in weight management and food intake regulation. Importance of physical activity in childhood, during pregnancy, in healthy adults and in improving functional capacity in the elderly

NUTR 505.Title: Public Health Nutrition
NUTR 505.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 505.Course_Description: This course focuses on the nutrition status of populations, communities and groups of people using a public health lens. It identifies and assesses human nutrition issues and problems, their causes, influencing factors and social conditions using a social determinants of health framework. Offers opportunities to design and conduct needs assessments, design and plan programs and plan for their evaluation. The purpose and role of participatory approaches with diverse populations and Indigenous populations in particular will be analyzed. Health systems, public health and political influence in Canada, as related to nutrition will be addressed

NUTR 506.Title: Qualitative Methods in Nutrition
NUTR 506.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 506.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
NUTR 506.Course_Description: Perspectives in study design, methods, and analysis. The application of qualitative research for developing, implementing, and evaluating community nutrition programs. Critiquing qualitative research articles and proposals for cultural safety and scientific rigour

NUTR 507.Title: Advanced Nutritional Biochemistry
NUTR 507.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 507.Course_Description: Specialized advanced topics in human nutrition, biochemistry and metabolism, including the dietary absorption and metabolism of iron, copper, and selenium and their role in energy metabolism, antioxidant defence, toxin elimination, and redox signaling and food source contamination, nutritional toxicology, and the negative impact these toxins have on metabolic networks and antioxidant defences

NUTR 508.Title: Professional Practice Stage 4A
NUTR 508.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 508.Course_Description: Directed professional practice experience in domains of clinical nutrition, management, nutrition education and/or community nutrition. This course includes at least one main clinical nutrition rotation, and may include additional weeks in other domains of practice

NUTR 509.Title: Professional Practice Stage 4B
NUTR 509.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 509.Course_Description: Directed professional practice experience in domains of clinical nutrition, management, nutrition education and/or community nutrition. This course includes management and community rotations

NUTR 511.Title: Nutrition and Behaviour
NUTR 511.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 511.Course_Description: This course will integrate biological, social and psychological determinants of eating and food choices in both health and disease. Topics will include behavioural theories relevant to eating and food choice, neurobiology of appetite regulation, mental health, obesity, chronic disease and effectiveness of behaviour-change intervention strategies

NUTR 512.Title: Herbs, Foods and Phytochemicals
NUTR 512.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 512.Prerequisites: Prerequisites (Undergraduate): FDSC 211 or LSCI 211 or BIOL 201 or BIOC 212
NUTR 512.Course_Description: An overview of the use of herbal medicines and food phytochemicals and the benefits and risks of their consumption. The physiological basis for activity and the assessment of toxicity will be presented. Current practices relating to the regulation, commercialization and promotion of herbs and phytochemicals will be considered

NUTR 515.Title: Dietetics French Examination
NUTR 515.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 515.Course_Description: Examination of French skills for the practice of dietetics. Testing will include definitions, comprehension of scientific articles, writing, conversation, and reading of and charting in medical records. Students are encouraged to take French courses as needed in the School of Continuing Studies or the French Language Centre at McGill

NUTR 537.Title: Advanced Human Metabolism
NUTR 537.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 537.Course_Description: Advanced topics in regulation and dysregulation of metabolism integrating mechanistic pre-clinical approaches to studying human health and disease. Presentation and critical analysis of metabolic research

NUTR 545.Title: Clinical Nutrition 2
NUTR 545.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 545.Course_Description: Pathophysiology and clinical nutrition intervention for various medical conditions. Topics include gastrointestinal disorders, surgery and nutrition support

NUTR 546.Title: Clinical Nutrition 3
NUTR 546.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 546.Course_Description: Clinical nutrition for diabetes, renal disease, eating disorders and other disorders in both adult and pediatric populations

NUTR 551.Title: Analysis of Nutrition Data
NUTR 551.Faculty: Human Nutrition (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
NUTR 551.Prerequisites: NUTR 337, AEMA 310 or another undergraduate-level statistics course
NUTR 551.Course_Description: Practical application of theoretical concepts in data analysis covering issues of study design, data collection, database organization, and statistical analysis using SPSS statistical software. Applications of statistical tests, reporting and interpretation of results, and data visualization

NUTR 603.Title: Credentialing in Dietetics
NUTR 603.Course_Description: Theoretical and practical integration of knowledge and skills required during graduate professional practice. Includes clinical assessment and nutritional monitoring techniques, analysis of interviewing and counseling situations, and application of management information systems and quality assurance procedures

NUTR 606.Title: Human Nutrition Research Methods
NUTR 606.Prerequisites: A course in nutrition across the lifespan at the intermediate undergraduate level such as NUTR 337, and a course in statistics at the graduate level, or permission of the instructor
NUTR 606.Course_Description: Methods in molecular biology and biochemistry and molecular techniques in nutrient metabolism, gene analysis, and metabolomics, experimental models for the human gut and metabolic diseases. Formation and criticism of designs for research, sampling techniques, measurement and analysis issues and human research ethics

NUTR 607.Title: Counselling in Professional Practice
NUTR 607.Course_Description: Techniques and strategies to enhance interpersonal skills for the health care environment. Topics include ethics, leadership and interprofessional teamwork. Hands-on practice in the dietitian's role as nutrition communicator, interviewer, counsellor, educator, motivator and behavioural change facilitator. Principles and practices essential to participating in entry-level dietetics

NUTR 608.Title: Special Topics 1
NUTR 608.Prerequisites: Permission of instructor and Director of School
NUTR 608.Course_Description: Prescribed reading, conference, lectures, assignments and/or practical work on selected topics in student's area of specialization. An approved course outline must be on file in the School's office prior to registration

NUTR 609.Title: Special Topics 2
NUTR 609.Prerequisites: Permission of instructor and Director of School
NUTR 609.Course_Description: An individualized course to allow students to undertake projects in library, laboratory, or field study. An approved course outline must be on file in the School's office prior to registration

NUTR 610.Title: Pediatric and Maternal Nutrition
NUTR 610.Course_Description: The scientific basis for topical and controversial issues during pregnancy, lactation and pediatric nutrition. Physiological, biochemical and molecular aspects of nutrient metabolism affecting maternal and pediatric health. Topics include molecular nutrition and birth defects, toxin-nutrient interactions and maldevelopment; epigenetics and metabolic programming; disrupted macro- and micronutrient metabolism and pregnancy complications; essential fatty acid metabolism and neural development; antioxidants, oxidative distress, inflammation and maternal and pediatric health

NUTR 611.Title: Graduate Professional Practice 1
NUTR 611.Course_Description: Dietetic practicum that includes the hospital environment, client-centred care and the patient experience. Communication, dietary assessment, nutrition education

NUTR 612.Title: Graduate Professional Practice 2 Management
NUTR 612.Course_Description: Assessment, planning, implementation, communication and evaluation in management of Food and Nutrition Systems. Focus is on application of management theory in dietetic practice

NUTR 613.Title: Graduate Professional Practice 3 Clinical Nutrition
NUTR 613.Course_Description: Initial rotation(s) in clinical nutrition. Assessment, planning, implementation, communication and evaluation of clinical nutrition care. Focus is on application of medical nutritional therapy for individuals and groups with a variety of disease states

NUTR 614.Title: Graduate Professional Practice 4 Community Nutrition
NUTR 614.Course_Description: Assessment, planning, implementation, communication, and evaluation of public health and community nutrition programs for a variety of individuals and population groups. Focus is on intervention strategies and their evaluation

NUTR 615.Title: Graduate Professional Practice 5 Clinical Nutrition
NUTR 615.Course_Description: Final rotation(s) in clinical nutrition. Assessment, planning, implementation, communication and evaluation of clinical nutrition care. Focus is on application of medical nutritional therapy for individuals and groups with a variety of disease states

NUTR 618.Title: Dietetics Professional Practice
NUTR 618.Course_Description: Introduction to the dietetics profession including ethics; provincial regulation; competencies and domains of practice; and dietetic practice in the hospital environment. Introductory activities related to food, food industry, agriculture, public health nutrition and clinical nutrition

NUTR 625.Title: Emerging Issues for Nutritionists
NUTR 625.Course_Description: Emerging issues in nutrition and dietetics relevant to professional practice. Emphasis on research and writing updates for professional practice documents. Effective oral communication skills with other allied health professionals, as well as the general public. A focus on online communication, evaluating and promoting accurate nutrition science appropriate for diverse target groups. Skills associated with professional leadership roles

NUTR 626.Title: Writing for Dietetics Practice
NUTR 626.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
NUTR 626.Course_Description: Identification and practice of effective writing techniques for the different types of writing likely to be required in dietetics practice, when taking a leadership role, promoting the profession, sharing knowledge and experience, and inspiring others. Writing for different segments of the general population, to writing for a professional audience. Peer critique and revision of text and design, in an effort to reach excellence, are important aspects of the course

NUTR 629.Title: Professional Dietetics Project
NUTR 629.Course_Description: A team project (3 or 4 students). Interventions and outcomes, or development and evaluation of tools and resources for dietetics practice, in a clinical or community nutrition setting, with individuals or groups as the target population. The project findings will be disseminated through a final report and a presentation to health professionals

NUTR 629D1.Title: Professional Dietetics Project
NUTR 629D1.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
NUTR 629D1.Course_Description: A team project (3 or 4 students). Interventions and outcomes, or development and evaluation of tools and resources for dietetics practice, in a clinical or community nutrition setting, with individuals or groups as the target population. The project findings will be disseminated through a final report and a presentation to health professionals

NUTR 629D2.Title: Professional Dietetics Project
NUTR 629D2.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
NUTR 629D2.Course_Description: A team project (3 or 4 students). Interventions and outcomes, or development and evaluation of tools and resources for dietetics practice, in a clinical or community nutrition setting, with individuals or groups as the target population. The project findings will be disseminated through a final report and a presentation to health professionals

NUTR 641.Title: Advanced Global Food Security
NUTR 641.Course_Description: Food security is a major concern on the international development agenda: hundreds of millions, and perhaps even billions of individuals still face food insecurity and hunger, even years after the Millennium Summit. This course is designed to provide graduate students with multidisciplinary tools in research and education required by practitioners and researchers to better assess, understand, and positively impact global food security. Students will attend the Annual McGill Global Food Security Conference, and will actively review presentations and interact with world experts from various sectors and disciplines presenting on cutting edge research and the state of Global Food Security

NUTR 651.Title: M.Sc. (Applied) Literature Review
NUTR 651.Prerequisites: NUTR 606, NUTR 695 Can also be taken as corequisites
NUTR 651.Course_Description: Review of literature and definition of problem/objective for the project or practicum

NUTR 658.Course_Description: Continuation of placement (4 weeks). Submission of placement report. This practicum relates to the Human Nutrition M.Sc. (Applied) degree

NUTR 659.Title: M.Sc. (Applied) Practicum 4
NUTR 659.Course_Description: Continuation of placement (4 weeks). Submission of placement report. This practicum relates to the Human Nutrition M.Sc. (Applied) degree

NUTR 660.Title: M.Sc.(Applied) Final Presentation
NUTR 660.Course_Description: Final oral presentation of the project or practicum

NUTR 680.Course_Description: Independent research under the direction of a supervisor toward completion of the M.Sc. thesis

NUTR 681.Title: Human Nutrition M.Sc. Thesis 2
NUTR 681.Course_Description: Independent research under the direction of a supervisor toward completion of the M.Sc. thesis. Presentation of a thesis proposal

ORGB 330.Title: People Analytics
ORGB 330.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): MGCR 271 or an equivalent introductory statistics class, and MGCR 222
ORGB 330.Course_Description: This is the era of big data. Companies and organizations are collecting an enormous amount of information and we are only just beginning to grasp the ways in which this information might be used. This course covers the emerging field of people analytics, which involves applying data collection and analysis techniques to improve the management of people within organizations. We will cover current people analytics techniques, common pitfalls, and possible shortcomings of people analytics, as well as the ethical questions involved in undertaking such analyses

ORGB 380.Title: Cross Cultural Management

Projects and simulations provide "hands-on" experience in the use of compensation techniques

ORGB 625.Title: Managing Organizational Change
ORGB 625.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ORGB 625.Course_Description: Examine strategies of organizational development (OD) that enhance the organization's capacity to respond to change, maximize productivity and allow employees to experience dignity and meaning in their work. Explores the strategic, techno-structural, human process, and human resource management types of OD interventions. In addition, the course will provide opportunities for the practice of various OD skills (process consultation, feedback, observation) which enable managers to identify dysfunctional policies or behaviours. The fundamental theoretical framework of the course will draw upon developments in the behavioural and socio-technical systems approaches to organizational change

ORGB 632.Title: Managing Teams in Organizations

The class environment used to accomplish this goal includes many exercises, personality inventories, and cases. The focus of the course will be on the processes of bargaining and the emphasis is "hands on" learning, although theories of negotiation and research examining negotiation will also be covered. Each student will have a great deal of control over how much he or she will develop into a better negotiator as a result of participating in this course

ORGB 634.Title: Career Development
ORGB 634.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
ORGB 634.Course_Description: The broad objective of this course is to increase students' understanding of the phenomenon of careers, in the business world as well as other spheres. Students will be exposed to "state of the art" theory and research on careers, and will then be expected to examine the usefulness and relevance of current theory by analyzing the careers of "real life" individuals, from novels, films, biographies, and case histories. The course will focus on the evolution of careers over time, and will consider in-depth the many factors which influence (and are influenced by) career development, including such things as individual characteristics and background: age and family, status; occupational, job, and organizational characteristics etc. Career development will be considered both from the perspective of the individual and the organization

PAED 401.Course_Description: The course will cover aspects of growth, perinatology, morbidity-mortality in pediatrics, infections in children, and neurologic, physical and psychological development. The course will include participation in the medical assessment and management of children, supplemented by didactic teaching and self-directed learning

PARA 410.Title: Environment and Infection
PARA 410.Prerequisites: one of LSCI 230, AEBI 211, ENVR 202, ENVB 305
PARA 410.Course_Description: Infectious pathogens of humans and animals and their impact on the global environment are considered. The central tenet is that infectious pathogens are environmental risk factors. The course considers their impact on the human condition and juxtaposes the impact of control and treatment measures and environmental change

PARA 424.Title: Fundamental Parasitology
PARA 424.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): AEBI 211 or LSCI 230 or permission of instructor
PARA 424.Course_Description: Systematics, morphology, biology and ecology of parasitic protozoa, flatworms, roundworms and arthropods with emphasis on economically and medically important species

PARA 438.Title: Immunology
PARA 438.Prerequisites: AEBI 202 or LSCI 202 or permission of instructor
PARA 438.Course_Description: An in-depth analysis of the principles of cellular and molecular immunology. The emphasis of the course is on host defence against infection and on diseases caused by abnormal immune responses

PARA 606.Title: Parasitology Seminar
PARA 606.Course_Description: A seminar series in which students present seminars covering topics in parasitology, in areas relevant to their research interests. Students register for the course in their second term of residency. Attendance and participation are compulsory for M.Sc. students

PARA 607.Title: Parasitology Research Seminar
PARA 607.Course_Description: This is a required course for M.Sc. students. A seminar course in which students registered at the Institute of Parasitology present seminars on the results of their thesis research. Students register for the course in the final term prior to thesis submission

PARA 635.Title: Cell Biology and Infection
PARA 635.Prerequisites: students with some background in molecular biology
PARA 635.Course_Description: Research articles will be the primary source of information. This course will cover new principles in cell biology. In particular, the mechanisms by which gene expression is regulated through signal transduction pathways initiated at the cell surface will be presented

PARA 645.Title: Applied Parasitology
PARA 645.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PARA 645.Prerequisites: 300-level undergraduate course in molecular biology, biochemistry or equivalent, or permission of instructor
PARA 645.Course_Description: Molecular aspects of applied parasitology. Diagnostics, surveillance, and epidemiology of parasites and the areas of anti-parasitic drug and vaccine development

PARA 655.Title: Pathogen Control Strategies
PARA 655.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PARA 655.Course_Description: An overview of one health including how infectious diseases caused by parasitic, viral, and bacterial pathogens are controlled in human and animal populations. With strong emphasis on drug discovery, development, production, approval, and deployment, examination of classical and emerging strategies for developing therapeutics, vaccines, biologics, and RNA-based agents. Exploration of how these interventions are identified, optimized, evaluated in preclinical and clinical settings, and implemented in real-world contexts shaped by epidemiology, resistance, and global health needs

PARA 665.Title: Special Topics in Parasitology
PARA 665.Course_Description: This course designation will be used for special courses that staff, or visiting professors, may wish to provide when student interest warrants. Examples might include a laboratory techniques course, a mathematical modelling course or a special pharmacology seminar series

PARA 678.Title: Microcirculation and Inflammation
PARA 678.Course_Description: Study of the structure of the microcirculation of several organs and basic mechanisms involved in the leukocyte-endothelium interaction in inflammation

PATH 300.Title: Human Disease
PATH 300.Prerequisites: BIOL 200, BIOL 201 or BIOC 212, PHGY 209. Pre-/co-requisite: PHGY 210
PATH 300.Course_Description: Provides a fundamental understanding of the diseases prevalent in North America, for upper level students in the biological sciences. Includes: general responses of cells and organ systems to injury; assessment of individual diseases by relating the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment and prevention to the primary biological abnormalities in each disorder

PATH 504.Title: Disease in Depth
PATH 504.Course_Description: Mechanisms controlling the cellular life cycle in normal versus disease states such as cancer, infectious disease, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and immune disorders

PATH 607.Title: Biochemical Pathology
PATH 607.Course_Description: Immunopathogenesis of Human Disease: Lectures and seminars on immune-regulatory mechanisms (cellular/molecular), maintaining the balance between protection and pathology; pathogenesis of major infectious diseases with bacterial, viral and parasitic involvement (e.g. tuberculosis, AIDS, malaria) and classical immune disorders (e.g. asthma)

PATH 652.Course_Description: Lectures and seminars dealing with concepts and current techniques in molecular biology applied to the study of human diseases with emphasis on cancer

PATH 653.Title: Reading and Conference
PATH 653.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PATH 653.Course_Description: Cytogenetics is the science and art of making and analyzing chromosome preparations. This course focuses on human chromosomes, although methodologies and principles apply broadly to other species as well. Basic facts and mysteries about chromosomes will be explained and discussed in the light of clinical examples

PHAR 200.Title: Introduction to Pharmacology 1
PHAR 200.Course_Description: The objective of this course is to give U1 Pharmacology Major program students an appreciation of research in Pharmacology. The focus will be on contributions of this research to our understanding of how drugs work, strategies towards the discovery of new drugs, and/or on how use of current drugs may be improved based on this understanding

PHAR 201.Title: Introduction to Pharmacology 2
PHAR 201.Course_Description: This course will be a continuation of PHAR 200 , taught in the fall semester. The focus will be on contributions of this research to our understanding of how drugs work, strategies towards the discovery of new drugs, and/or on how use of current drugs may be improved based on this understanding

PHAR 300.Title: Drug Action
PHAR 300.Prerequisites: BIOL 200, PHGY 209, PHGY 210 and one of BIOL 201 or ANAT/BIOC 212 or permission of instructor
PHAR 300.Course_Description: Principles of pharmacology and toxicology. Frequently encountered drugs will be used as a focus to illustrate sites and mechanisms of action, distribution, metabolism, elimination and adverse side effects

PHAR 301.Title: Drugs and Disease
PHAR 301.Course_Description: This course further explores the basic principles of pharmacology as illustrated by drugs used in the treatment of disease. Emphasis is placed on drugs used for diseases prevalent in North America

PHAR 303.Title: Principles of Toxicology
PHAR 303.Prerequisites: BIOL 200, BIOL 201 or BIOC 212, PHGY 209 and PHGY 210
PHAR 303.Course_Description: Fundamental mechanisms by which toxic compounds damage a biological system (organelle, cell, organ, organism, ecosystem). Detection and quantification of toxicity and risk/benefit analysis are considered. Selected agents of current risk to human health or the environment are evaluated in depth

PHAR 390.Title: Laboratory in Pharmacology
PHAR 390.Course_Description: This course is a two-week all day practical laboratory course where students will have the opportunity to design their own experiments, write out the experimental lab reports and learn to trouble shoot on their own

PHAR 396.Title: Undergraduate Research Project
PHAR 396.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): Completion of at least one undergraduate term with CGPA of 3.0
PHAR 396.Course_Description: Independent research project with a final written report and an oral presentation

PHAR 397.Title: Pharmacology Research Project 2
PHAR 397.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHAR 397.Prerequisites: Successful completion of PHAR 396, a CGPA of at least 3.0, and permission of the instructor
PHAR 397.Course_Description: Research project to be carried out under supervision of a faculty member in the Department of Pharmacology and Therapeutics. Projects should address a testable hypothesis to be tested using the experimental tools available in the supervisor’s lab and probably other facilities at McGill. Hands-on experience with contemporary research in pharmacology and related disciplines

PHAR 503.Title: Drug Discovery and Development 1
PHAR 503.Prerequisites: PHAR 301 or PHAR 303; or permission of instructor
PHAR 503.Course_Description: Chemistry, mechanisms of action, and steps in drug discovery and development

PHAR 504.Title: Drug Discovery and Development 2
PHAR 504.Prerequisites: PHAR 301 or PHAR 303; or permission of instructor
PHAR 504.Course_Description: Nobel Prize-winning discoveries as a basis for drug development

PHAR 505.Title: Structural Pharmacology
PHAR 505.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): PHAR 301, BIOC 311 or with permission of instructor
PHAR 505.Course_Description: The course will cover approaches widely used in the pharmaceuticals industry, such as drug target selection, structure determination and medicinal chemistry. The basics of structural biology will be taught in a very visual and interactive manner, with an emphasis on drug:target interactions and chemical principles relevant to drug design. By the end of the course, the students will become familiar with the structure-based drug discovery process and principles of molecular pharmacology

PHAR 508.Title: Drug Discovery and Development 3
PHAR 508.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): PHAR 301 (PHAR 503 or PHAR 505 are also highly recommended)
PHAR 508.Course_Description: The design of biologically-relevant drug screens for molecular targets in a cell, tissue, and in vivo setting. Explore the use of stem cells and tissue-based disease models for the understanding of disease and for drug discovery. Situate modern pharmacology into broader medical and societal issues such as personalized medicine and the ethics associated with research

PHAR 510.Title: New Advances in Antimicrobial
PHAR 510.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHAR 510.Course_Description: Overview on bacteria, insights into bacterial pathogenesis, an understanding of antibiotics, and new developments in antibacterial to beat antibiotic resistance

PHAR 522D1.Title: Fundamentals of Disease Therapy
PHAR 522D1.Faculty: Pharmacology and Therapeutics (Faculty of Medicine & Hlth Sci)
PHAR 522D1.Prerequisites: FMED 525 or permission of the instructor
PHAR 522D1.Course_Description: Basic physiology and pathology, including a macro-level overview of normal physiology and pathophysiology of selected organs

PHAR 522D2.Title: Fundamentals of Disease Therapy
PHAR 522D2.Faculty: Pharmacology and Therapeutics (Faculty of Medicine & Hlth Sci)
PHAR 522D2.Prerequisites: FMED 525 or permission of the instructor

PHAR 524.Title: Clinical Mentorship
PHAR 524.Faculty: Pharmacology and Therapeutics (Faculty of Medicine & Hlth Sci)
PHAR 524.Prerequisites: FMED 525 or permission of the instructor
PHAR 524.Course_Description: Interaction with clinicians and clinician scientists in the field of medicine and health sciences, focusing on understanding disease from their perspective

PHAR 540.Title: Advances in Industrial Biotechnology
PHAR 540.Prerequisites: CHEM 222 (or equivalent) and BIOL 200 or CHEM 332
PHAR 540.Course_Description: Introduction to emerging technologies and research advances in biotechnologies. Topics include semisynthetic production of drugs and drug candidates through large-scale fermentation, next generation synthesis of DNA and whole genes, green toxicology, single-molecule diagnostics, orphan-drug re-purposing, and next- generation genomic analyses in drug development. Translational research, issues of entrepreneurship, sustainability, and ethics are also covered

PHAR 562.Title: Neuropharmacology
PHAR 562.Prerequisites: PHAR 301 or with permission of instructor
PHAR 562.Course_Description: Topics in pharmacology with an emphasis on molecular mechanisms of drug-action and cellular targets in the nervous system

PHAR 563.Title: Endocrine Pharmacology
PHAR 563.Prerequisites: PHAR 301 or permission of the instructor(s)
PHAR 563.Course_Description: This advanced course covers selected topics in pharmacology of reproductive, endocrine, and metabolic disorders

PHAR 565.Title: Epigenetic Drugs and Targets
PHAR 565.Course_Description: This course covers therapeutics targeting epigenetic mechanisms. Although only a handful of epigenetic drugs are in widespread use, further development of such agents is a very active area of research as it has the potential to directly target aberrant gene expression. This course will examine both the current use and potential of epigenetic drugs in treatment of cancer, neurological diseases, immune disorders, and cardiovascular disease. The concept of epigenetics as mediating gene-environment interaction will also be discussed

PHAR 590.Title: Advanced Research Methods in Pharmacology
PHAR 590.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHAR 590.Prerequisites: PHAR 390, or permission of the instructor
PHAR 590.Corequisites: PHAR 599 or PHAR 598, or permission of the instructor
PHAR 590.Course_Description: Investigation into the signaling, regulation and modulation of a large family of receptors of fundamental importance in pharmacology

PHAR 598.Course_Description: Supervised Honours Research Project in Pharmacology. Students are expected to obtain hands-on research experience in their supervisor's laboratory. They are also required to submit a written report in the form of a scientific manuscript and present a ten minute seminar

PHAR 602.Course_Description: Overview of core principles in pharmacology, with an emphasis on advanced concepts and state-of-the-art current research. Molecular mechanisms for interactions of drugs with their receptors, pharmacokinetics, drug design, and toxicology

PHAR 609.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): Any Pharmacology 500 level excluding PHAR 598 and 599
PHAR 609.Course_Description: Discussion of good research practices in Pharmacology, including scientific conduct and misconduct, mentorship, authorship, peer review, research on animal and human subjects, and intellectual property

PHAR 610.Course_Description: This is a hands-on course with a strong emphasis on developing scientific writing and oral communication skills in Pharmacology

PHGY 209.Title: Mammalian Physiology 1
PHGY 209.Prerequisites: BIOL 112, CHEM 110, CHEM 120, PHYS 101 or PHYS 131, and PHYS 102 or PHYS 142. Pre-/co-requisites: BIOL 200, CHEM 212 or equivalent
PHGY 209.Course_Description: Physiology of body fluids, blood, body defense mechanisms, muscle, peripheral, central, and autonomic nervous systems

PHGY 210.Title: Mammalian Physiology 2
PHGY 210.Prerequisites: BIOL 112, CHEM 110, CHEM 120, PHYS 101 or PHYS 131, and PHYS 102 or PHYS 142. Pre-/co-requisite: BIOL 200, BIOL 201, BIOC 212, CHEM 212 or equivalent
PHGY 210.Course_Description: Physiology of cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, endocrine and renal systems

PHGY 212.Course_Description: Exercises illustrating fundamental principles in physiology: Biological Signals Acquisitions, Blood, Immunology, Neurophysiology, Neuromuscular Physiology

PHGY 213.Title: Introductory Physiology Laboratory 2
PHGY 213.Course_Description: Exercises illustrating fundamental principles in physiology: Central Nervous System, Cardiovascular, Respiration, Exercise Physiology, Molecular Endocrinology

PHGY 311.Title: Channels, Synapses and Hormones
PHGY 311.Prerequisites: PHGY 209 or permission of the instructor
PHGY 311.Course_Description: In-depth presentation of experimental results and hypotheses on cellular communication in the nervous system and the endocrine system

PHGY 312.Title: Respiratory, Renal, and Cardiovascular Physiology
PHGY 312.Prerequisites: PHGY 209 and PHGY 210 or equivalent, PHGY 311 or permission of the instructor
PHGY 312.Course_Description: In-depth presentation of experimental results and hypotheses underlying our current understanding of topics in renal, respiratory and cardiovascular functions explored beyond the introductory level

PHGY 313.Title: Blood, Gastrointestinal, and Immune Systems Physiology
PHGY 313.Prerequisites: PHGY 209 and PHGY 210 or equivalent, PHGY 311 or permission of the instructor
PHGY 313.Course_Description: In-depth presentation of experimental results and hypotheses underlying our current understanding of topics in immunology, blood and fluids, and gastrointestinal physiology

PHGY 314.Title: Integrative Neuroscience
PHGY 314.Course_Description: In depth presentation of experimental results and hypotheses underlying our current understanding of how single neurons and ensembles of neurons encode sensory information, generate movement, and control cognitive functions such as emotion, learning, and memory, during voluntary behaviours

PHGY 351.Title: Research Techniques: Physiology
PHGY 351.Course_Description: Provides an overview of common research methods in Physiology, including critical analysis and practical experience with some of the methods. Topics include research ethics of animal experimentation, data analysis, membrane biophysics, radioimmunoassay, ion sensitive dyes, immunocytochemistry, localization techniques, protein transport, cell sorting and molecular biology

PHGY 359D1.Title: Tutorial in Physiology
PHGY 359D1.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHGY 359D1.Course_Description: The course consists of regularly scheduled meetings between each individual student and a chosen staff member, to consider current problems in biomedical research and to develop background for a research project to be carried out in U3. Brief written summaries of each meeting are required

PHGY 359D2.Title: Tutorial in Physiology

PHGY 419D1.Course_Description: Individual research projects in immunology under the guidance of staff members in the three participating departments: Physiology, Biochemistry, and Microbiology and Immunology

PHGY 425.Title: Analyzing Physiological Systems
PHGY 425.Prerequisites: PHGY 311, PHGY 314, BIOL 200 or permission from instructor
PHGY 425.Course_Description: An introduction to quantitative analysis of physiological data, both to the mode of thinking and to a set of tools that allows accurate predictions of biological systems. Examples will range from oscillating genetic networks to understanding higher brain function. Modelling and data analysis through examples and exercises will be emphasized

PHGY 451.Title: Advanced Neurophysiology
PHGY 451.Course_Description: Topics of current interest in neurophysiology including the development of neurons and synapses, physiology of ionic channels, presynaptic and postsynaptic events in synaptic transmission and neuronal interactions in CNS function

PHGY 459D1.Title: Physiology Seminar
PHGY 459D1.Course_Description: Discussion of topics in mammalian, cellular and molecular physiology. Students will be required to write one essay and make at least one oral presentation per term. A final course essay is required

PHGY 461D1.Title: Experimental Physiology
PHGY 461D1.Course_Description: Individual project work under the supervision of Departmental Staff members

PHGY 461D2.Title: Experimental Physiology
PHGY 461D2.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.

PHGY 488.Title: Stem Cell Biology
PHGY 488.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): PHGY 313 or by permission of instructor
PHGY 488.Course_Description: The main concepts in stem cell biology: embryonic stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells, cancer stem cells, stem cells populations of many adult tissues, applications of stem cell biology and ethical issues surrounding stem cell use in research and medicine. The major experimental methods and laboratory techniques in stem cell biology

PHGY 499.Title: Independent Study in Physiology
PHGY 499.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHGY 499.Prerequisites: PHGY 311, PHGY 312, PHGY 313, PHGY 314. Note: A form from the Student Affairs Officer, Room 1022, McIntyre Medical Bldg., must be completed prior to registration

PHGY 502.Title: Exercise Physiology
PHGY 502.Course_Description: Behaviour of physiological processes in response to physical effort, in areas such as structural basis of muscle contraction, thermoregulation during exercise, mechanics and energetics of muscle contraction, fuel utilization, fatigue, physiological adjustments during exercise and influence of training

PHGY 508.Title: Advanced Renal Physiology
PHGY 508.Course_Description: Advanced concepts in selected areas of kidney physiology, including the glomerulus, renal cell biology, kidney development, membrane and epithelial transport, hormones and autacoids, kidney transplantation, bioengineering and regenerative medicine

PHGY 513.Title: Translational Immunology
PHGY 513.Prerequisites: MIMM 314 or PHGY 313 or permission of the instructor
PHGY 513.Course_Description: Advanced key concepts in immunology as they relate to health and disease, including infectious diseases, non-infectious diseases and autoimmunity, and cancer immunology

PHGY 515.Title: Blood-Brain Barrier in Health and Disease
PHGY 515.Prerequisites: PHGY 313 or PHGY 314 and permission of the instructor
PHGY 515.Course_Description: Molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the organization and regulation of the blood-brain barrier, highlighting neurological diseases associated with the blood-brain barrier breakdown and give an overview of experimental approaches to study blood-brain barrier

PHGY 516.Title: Physiology of Blood
PHGY 516.Course_Description: Bone marrow hematopoiesis, with emphasis on regulation of stem cell proliferation and differentiation along hematopoietic pathways. Formation and differentiation of red and white blood cells and some of the diseases associated with hematopoiesis will be covered. Emphasis will be given to the molecular mechanisms involved in the normal and pathological conditions

PHGY 518.Title: Artificial Cells
PHGY 518.Course_Description: Physiology, biotechnology, chemistry and biomedical application of artificial cells, blood substitutes, immobilized enzymes, microorganisms and cells, hemoperfusion, artificial kidneys, and drug delivery systems. PHGY 517 and PHGY 518 when taken together, will give a complete picture of this field. However, the student can select one of these

PHGY 520.Title: Ion Channels
PHGY 520.Course_Description: A discussion of the principal theories and interesting new developments in the study of ion channels. Based on a textbook, computer exercises and critical reading and presentation of research papers. Topics include: Properties of voltage-and ligand-gated channels, single channel analysis, structure and function of ion channels

PHGY 524.Title: Chronobiology
PHGY 524.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHGY 524.Prerequisites: PHGY 209 and PHGY 210 (or NSCI 200 and NSCI 201), and a relevant 300-level course (PHGY 311, or PHGY 314, or PSYC 318, or BIOC 311, or other, with permission of course coordinator)
PHGY 524.Course_Description: An introduction to the field of chronobiology. The aim is to provide basic instruction on different types of biological rhythms, with particular focus on circadian rhythms

PHGY 525.Title: Cortical Plasticity
PHGY 525.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHGY 525.Prerequisites: NSCI 200 or PHGY 314 or permission of the instructor
PHGY 525.Course_Description: An examination of cortical plasticity following peripheral and central nervous damage from a systems/cognitive neuroscience perspective. Focus is on sensory systems and animal models, including the following topics: ocular dominance columns, retinal lesions, blindness, deafness, cochlear implants, barrel fields, amputation, stroke, and hemispherectomy. Experimental approaches to be considered include: electrophysiological recording, psychophysics, behaviour, and functional imaging

PHGY 531.Title: Topics in Applied Immunology
PHGY 531.Course_Description: Seminar format course in which experts in immunologic mechanisms of resistance against a variety of infectious diseases, including AIDS, malaria, and tuberculosis oversee student moderators in their presentation of recent scientific literature in the field

PHGY 550.Title: Molecular Physiology of Bone
PHGY 550.Course_Description: Students will develop a working knowledge of cartilage and bone. Discussion topics will include: molecular and cellular environment of bone; heritable and acquired skeletal defects; research models used to study metabolic bone disease

PHGY 552.Title: Cellular and Molecular Physiology
PHGY 552.Course_Description: Discussions of recent significant advances in our understanding of the gene products involved in diverse cellular signalling pathways. Topics will include cell-surface hormone receptors, nuclear steroid hormone receptors, and ion channels and transporters. Students will present and critically evaluate experimental approaches, results and interpretations of selected research publications

PHGY 556.Title: Topics in Systems Neuroscience

PHIL 197.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.

PHIL 198.Title: FYS: Knowledge and Ideas in Early Modern Philosophy
PHIL 198.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 198.Course_Description: An introduction to central issues in the philosophy of the early modern period through an examination of works by, for example, Descartes, Malebranche, Spinoza, Locke, Leibniz, Berkeley and Hume

PHIL 199.Title: FYS: Minds, Brain, and Machines
PHIL 199.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 199.Course_Description: An introduction to the philosophical foundations of the sciences of the mind

PHIL 200.Title: Introduction to Philosophy 1
PHIL 200.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 200.Course_Description: A course treating some of the central problems of philosophy: the mind-body problem, freedom, scepticism and certainty, fate, time, and the existence of God

PHIL 201.Title: Introduction to Philosophy 2
PHIL 201.Course_Description: An introduction to some of the major problems of philosophy. This course does not duplicate PHIL 200

PHIL 202.Title: The Good Life
PHIL 202.Course_Description: Explores how philosophers from Socrates to Sartre wrestle with the question of how we should live, including ancient philosophers who present their teachings as pathways to happiness, virtue, and peace of mind; medieval philosophers who seek to understand God’s will; and modern philosophers who grapple with the tension between community and freedom. Analyzes debates of fundamental moral and existential questions: What things really matter? Does it pay to be good? What constitutes the best society? Can we escape the roller coaster of our emotions? Examines how answers are intertwined with beliefs about God, nature, knowledge, the soul, and politics

PHIL 203.Title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Ethics
PHIL 203.Course_Description: An introduction to several important debates in the ethics of artificial intelligence (AI), including: artificial general intelligence, artificial consciousness, existential risk, and the moral status of advanced AI systems, to practical ethical and political issues raised by the uses of AI systems, including opacity, discrimination, privacy,disinformation and impacts on work and wealth distribution

PHIL 210.Title: Introduction to Deductive Logic 1
PHIL 210.Course_Description: An introduction to propositional and predicate logic; formalization of arguments, truth tables, systems of deduction, elementary metaresults, and related topics

PHIL 221.Title: Introduction to History and Philosophy of Science 2
PHIL 221.Course_Description: A survey of the development of modern science since the Eighteenth Century

PHIL 230.Title: Introduction to Moral Philosophy 1
PHIL 230.Course_Description: A survey of a number of historically important and influential theories. Philosophers to be discussed may include Aristotle, Hume, Kant, Bentham, Mill, and Moore

PHIL 237.Title: Contemporary Moral Issues
PHIL 237.Course_Description: An introductory discussion of central ethical questions (the value of persons, or the relationship of rights and utilities, for example) through the investigation of currently disputed social and political issues. Specific issues to be discussed may include pornography and censorship, affirmative action, civil disobedience, punishment, abortion, and euthanasia

PHIL 240.Title: Political Philosophy 1
PHIL 240.Course_Description: An introduction to contemporary philosophy of politics by concentrating on a number of contested concepts, such as freedom, justice and equality, in contemporary political philosophy and practice

PHIL 242.Title: Introduction to Feminist Theory
PHIL 242.Course_Description: An introduction to feminist theory as political theory. Emphasis is placed on the plurality of analyses and proposals that constitute contemporary feminist thought. Some of the following are considered: liberal feminism, marxist and socialist feminism, radical feminism, postmodern feminism, francophone feminism, and the contributions to feminist theory by women of colour and lesbians

PHIL 301.Title: Philosophical Fundamentals
PHIL 301.Prerequisites: two previous courses in philosophy, one of which must be PHIL 210 or written consent of the Department
PHIL 301.Course_Description: An intensive study of basic philosophical skills; reading, writing, analysis, and argumentation

PHIL 306.Title: Philosophy of Mind
PHIL 306.Course_Description: A survey of major positions of the mind-body problem, focusing on such questions as: Do we have minds and bodies? Can minds affect bodies? Is mind identical to body? If so, in what sense "identical"? Can physical bodies be conscious

PHIL 310.Title: Intermediate Logic
PHIL 310.Course_Description: A second course in Logic. NB. The course will be technical in nature, and some mathematical aptitude is essential. The emphasis is on the expressive properties of standard logical systems, including implications for the philosophy of mathematics. We will study the Completeness of First-Order Logic, then the 'limitative' theorems of Tarski and Gödel

PHIL 311.Title: Philosophy of Mathematics
PHIL 311.Course_Description: This course provides an historically informed introduction to philosophy of mathematics. It gives the student an overview of prominent issues and arguments, to enable her to follow and discuss contemporary research in philosophy of mathematics

PHIL 327.Title: Philosophy of Race
PHIL 327.Course_Description: An introduction to issues in the philosophy of race, for example: the metaphysical status of race; the biology of racial categories; the social construction of race; the relationship between race and racism; the phenomenology of racialized subjectivity; or, intersections of race, gender, and other identity categories

PHIL 334.Title: Ethical Theory
PHIL 334.Prerequisites: one of PHIL 230, PHIL 237, PHIL 242, PHIL 343, or written permission of the instructor
PHIL 334.Course_Description: A course focusing on central questions in ethical theory such as the nature of the good and the right and the factors which determine moral rightness and wrongness

PHIL 336.Title: Aesthetics
PHIL 336.Course_Description: An introduction to issues central to aesthetic theory; the nature of aesthetic judgment, perception of the aesthetic object, the nature of the art object

PHIL 341.Title: Philosophy of Science 1
PHIL 341.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 341.Course_Description: A discussion of philosophical problems as they arise in the context of scientific practice and enquiry. Such issues as the philosophical presuppositions of the physical and social sciences, the nature of scientific method and its epistemological implications will be addressed

PHIL 343.Title: Biomedical Ethics
PHIL 343.Course_Description: An investigation of ethical issues as they arise in the practice of medicine (informed consent, e.g.) or in the application of medical technology (in vitro fertilization, euthanasia, e.g.)

PHIL 344.Title: Medieval and Renaissance Political Theory
PHIL 344.Course_Description: A study of Medieval and Renaissance political theory

PHIL 345.Title: Greek Political Theory
PHIL 345.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 345.Course_Description: An examination of the ethical and political theories of ancient Greece, especially those of Plato and Aristotle

PHIL 348.Title: Philosophy of Law 1
PHIL 348.Course_Description: A discussion of the nature of justice and law, and of the relationship between them

PHIL 349.Title: Environmental Philosophy
PHIL 349.Course_Description: An introduction to environmental ethics; potentially also such related fields as philosophy of ecology, environmental aesthetics, and/or other philosophical topics demonstrably relevant to environmental issues

PHIL 350.Title: History and Philosophy of Ancient Science
PHIL 350.Course_Description: Topics in ancient pure mathematics (geometry and number theory), "mixed mathematics" (astronomy, music theory, optics, mechanics), and/or natural science (including medicine), studied with a view to philosophical issues raised by the content of ancient science and/or by the logic of scientific argument

PHIL 353.Title: The Presocratic Philosophers
PHIL 353.Course_Description: An examination of the surviving fragments of the presocratic philosophers and schools of philosophy, as well as later reports of their views

PHIL 354.Title: Plato
PHIL 354.Course_Description: An examination of some of the philosophical problems (those in logic, epistemology, metaphysics, and ethics, e.g.) found in a selection of Plato's dialogues

PHIL 355.Title: Aristotle
PHIL 355.Course_Description: An examination of selected works by Aristotle. The course considers issues in moral philosophy as well as those found in the logical treatises, the Physics and Metaphysics, and in the philosophy of mind

PHIL 356.Title: Early Medieval Philosophy
PHIL 356.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 356.Course_Description: An examination of selected works in the Christian, Islamic and Jewish traditions. Topics in moral and political philosophy, logic and metaphysics, philosophical psychology and epistemology, philosophy of science, and philosophical theology may be discussed

PHIL 360.Title: 17th Century Philosophy
PHIL 360.Course_Description: An examination of the work of such seventeenth-century philosophers as Descartes, Hobbes, Gassendi, Malebranche, Leibniz, and the Cambridge Platonists

PHIL 361.Title: 18th Century Philosophy
PHIL 361.Course_Description: A survey of eighteenth century philosophy, especially British philosophy. Attention is given to fundamental metaphysical, epistemological, and moral issues as reflected in the work of such philosophers as Locke, Shaftesbury, Berkeley, Hutcheson, Butler, Hume and Reid

PHIL 366.Title: 18th and Early 19th Century German Philosophy
PHIL 366.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 366.Course_Description: An examination of the works of such philosophers as Kant, Fichte, Jacobi, Schelling, and Hegel

PHIL 367.Title: 19th Century Philosophy
PHIL 367.Prerequisites: A previous course in philosophy is recommended
PHIL 367.Course_Description: An examination of the works of such 19th century philosophers as Mach, Helmholtz, Dedekind, Frege, Marx, Kierkegaard, Schopenhauer, Nietzsche, Mill and Bradley

PHIL 375.Title: Existentialism
PHIL 375.Course_Description: This course will examine the nature of existentialist thought as represented in various philosophical and literary texts. Particular themes to be examined include freedom, alienation, responsibility and choice, and the nature of self

PHIL 411.Course_Description: A course focusing on some philosophical issue (e.g., the nature of numbers or the relation of truth to provability) as it arises in the study of mathematics and logic

PHIL 415.Title: Philosophy of Language
PHIL 415.Prerequisites: PHIL 210 or equivalent and one intermediate course in philosophy
PHIL 415.Course_Description: An examination of central notions in the philosophy of language (reference, meaning, and truth, e.g.), the puzzles these notions give rise to, and the relevance of these notions to such questions as: What is language? How is communication possible? What is understanding? Is language rule-governed

PHIL 419.Title: Epistemology
PHIL 419.Prerequisites: PHIL 210 or equivalent and one intermediate course in philosophy
PHIL 419.Course_Description: A discussion of central topics in the theory of knowledge. The questions addressed in the course may include: What is knowledge? Do we have any knowledge? What is the relation between knowledge and belief? When is belief justified? Is all knowledge conscious knowledge

PHIL 421.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHIL 421.Prerequisites: PHIL 210 or equivalent and one intermediate course in philosophy
PHIL 421.Course_Description: An examination of central questions in metaphysics in their historical and contemporary forms. Topics may be chosen from such issues as: personal identity, the nature of space and time, the nature of events and properties, possible worlds, and the problem of realism

PHIL 427.Title: Topics in Critical Philosophy of Race

PHTH 245.Title: Introduction to Professional Practice 1
PHTH 245.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 245.Course_Description: Physical therapy and its domains through promoting health and well-being of individuals across the life span

PHTH 301.Title: Sports Medicine Practicum
PHTH 301.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 301.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
PHTH 301.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): PHTH 245; ANAT 315; PHGY 209; ANAT 316; PHGY 210; POTH 225; POTH 250. Students require a valid CPR-AED level HCP certificate before the practical work begins. Required interviews and selection process for this course will be conducted by the McGill Sport Medicine Clinic staff
PHTH 301.Course_Description: This course is intended to provide students with a directed, practical experience in pre-event, on-field and post-event sports therapy interventions. Students will be introduced to current concepts in sports medicine. Students will work closely with at least one of the McGill varsity teams, as well as intra- and interprofessionally with the staff of the McGill Sport Medicine Clinic (including physiotherapists, athletic therapists, physicians, and other allied health-care professionals)

PHTH 301D1.Title: Sports Medicine Practicum
PHTH 301D1.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 301D1.Prerequisites: PHTH 245; ANAT 315; PHGY 209; ANAT 316; PHGY 210; POTH 225; POTH 250. Students require a valid CPR-AED level HCP certificate before the practical work begins. Required interviews and selection process for this course will be conducted by the McGill Sport Medicine Clinic staff

PHTH 301D2.Title: Sports Medicine Practicum
PHTH 301D2.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 301D2.Prerequisites: PHTH 301D1 and PHTH 245; ANAT 315; PHGY 209; ANAT 316; PHGY 210; POTH 225; POTH 250. Students require a valid CPR-AED level HCP certificate before the practical work begins. Required interviews and selection process for this course will be conducted by the McGill Sport Medicine Clinic staff

PHTH 440.Title: Clinical Exercise Physiology
PHTH 440.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 440.Course_Description: Safe and effective prescription of exercise as a preventive and therapeutic tool in patients suffering from clinical conditions

PHTH 450.Title: Introduction to PT Clinical Practice
PHTH 450.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 450.Course_Description: In this course, students will be introduced to clinical skills applicable to various physiotherapy domains of practice. Through clinical skills laboratories, self-directed learning, and interactive learning sessions, students will be developing observation skills, as well as analyzing normal and common deviant movements. They will also be introduced to the development of hypotheses to explain movement impairment. Throughout the course, emphasis will be put on palpation and patient handling skills

PHTH 460.Title: Introduction to Functional Movement
PHTH 460.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 460.Course_Description: Introduction to the assessment and instruction of human functional movement patterns, including anatomy, physiology, and biomechanics. Principles of progressive functional resistance training

PHTH 482.Title: Introduction to Health, Fitness and Lifestyle
PHTH 482.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 482.Course_Description: Introduction to lifestyle concepts and practices, complementary to the scope of physiotherapy practice, which influence individual health and fitness. Topics include: physical activity, sedentary behaviour, diet, sleep, and psychological and mental wellbeing. Certain external factors that influence these concepts and practices, and approaches to promoting behavioural change

PHTH 505D1.Title: Physical Therapy Clinical Practicum Seminars
PHTH 505D1.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 505D1.Course_Description: How the seven entry to practice domains play out in clinical practice, including the resources available while on placement. The clinical education program requirements and preparatory activities, feedback and conflict management, the evaluation process concerning practice domains, the role of the Ordre professionnel de la Physiotherapie du Québec, and different associations in physiotherapy

PHTH 505D2.Title: Physical Therapy Clinical Practicum Seminars
PHTH 505D2.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 505D2.Course_Description: How the seven entry to practice domains play out in clinical practice, including the resources available while on placement. The clinical education program requirements and preparatory activities, feedback and conflict management, the evaluation process concerning practice domains, the role of the Ordre professionnel de la Physiotherapie du Québec, and different associations in physiotherapy

PHTH 550.Title: Physical Therapy Orthopedic Management
PHTH 550.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 550.Prerequisites: ANAT 315 or EDKP 206 or equivalent, EDKP 395 or equivalent as judged by the admission process
PHTH 550.Course_Description: Evaluation and treatment in a neuromuscular framework

PHTH 551.Title: Physical Therapy Neurological Rehabilitation
PHTH 551.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 551.Prerequisites: ANAT 321, POTH 455. Restriction: Not open to students who have taken OCC1 335 and PHTH 338
PHTH 551.Course_Description: Principles of neurorehabilitation motor learning and neuroplasticity including assessment and treatment

PHTH 554.Title: PT Cardiorespiratory Rehabilitation
PHTH 554.Faculty: Phys and Occ Therapy (School of Phys & Occ Therapy)
PHTH 554.Prerequisites: ANAT 316, PHTH 225, PHTH 440, PHGY 209, or equivalent as judged by the admission process
