WCOM 203.Title: Introduction to Creative Writing
WCOM 203.Course_Description: Production of original creative works in English. Study and application of writing techniques and craft elements observed in both traditional and contemporary forms, ranging from poetic forms such as the sonnet, the villanelle, and free verse,to short fiction forms such as the short story and the vignette, to hybrid forms such as prose poetry and flash fiction. Craft, analysis of literary texts, workshop-style critique, and multiple drafts

WCOM 206.Title: Communication in Engineering
WCOM 206.Course_Description: Written and oral communication in Engineering (in English): strategies for generating, developing, organizing, and presenting ideas in a technical setting; problem-solving; communicating to different audiences; editing and revising; and public speaking. Course work based on academic, technical, and professional writing in engineering

WCOM 225.Title: ESL: Foundations of Academic English
WCOM 225.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 225.Course_Description: Focus on core academic English competencies at the intermediate level, including sentence structure, grammar, cohesion, paragraph development, and academic vocabulary. Introduces short academic texts and foundational writing and communication practices, alongside strategies for note-taking, vocabulary building, editing, and oral presentation structure. Provides essential linguistic skills for engaging in academic communication and more advanced writing contexts

WCOM 235.Title: ESL: Academic Writing and Communication Competencies
WCOM 235.Prerequisites: CESL 200 or WCOM 225 or placement test
WCOM 235.Course_Description: Focus on upper-intermediate academic English competencies through extended paragraphing, short essays, and genre-based writing. Emphasizes academic vocabulary development, grammatical accuracy in common academic structures, rhetorical organization, and effective communication across academic contexts.Foundational source integration and presentation skills in more complex university-level writing and communicative tasks

WCOM 245.Title: ESL: Essay and Critical Thinking
WCOM 245.Prerequisites: CESL 300 or WCOM 235 or placement test
WCOM 245.Course_Description: Academic writing skills and communicative competence in English at the upper-intermediate level. Critical thinking and reading applied to the whole writing process. Focus on integrating sources, creating effective arguments, and understanding essay structure and paragraph essentials. Academic genres: summary, paraphrase, quotation, and critique. Review of writing mechanics and grammar

WCOM 250.Title: Research Essay and Rhetoric
WCOM 250.Course_Description: Academic research-based writing across the disciplines. Article summary, critical analysis, rhetorical strategies, citation and paraphrase of academic sources, and editing for cohesion and clarity

WCOM 255.Title: ESL: Research Essay and Rhetoric
WCOM 255.Prerequisites: CESL 400 or WCOM 245 or placement test
WCOM 255.Course_Description: Principles and use of academic research skills to generate academic writing at an advanced level of English across the disciplines. Focus on article summary, critical analysis, and logical reasoning to develop sound arguments and well-reasoned essays. Common rhetorical strategies, citation and paraphrase of academic sources, and editing skills to enhance cohesion and avoid common English-as-a-Second Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax, and vocabulary

WCOM 295.Title: ESL: Academic Skills
WCOM 295.Course_Description: The university classroom: note-taking and summary of lectures; paraphrase and summary of written and multimedia materials; oral and seminar presentations; ethical use of Artificial Intelligence/Large Language Models. Critical thinking, reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills and strategies

WCOM 300.Title: Writing and Community Action
WCOM 300.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 300.Course_Description: Exploration of the relationship between experiential writing and community engagement. Instruction in and application of principles of writing pedagogy (in English) and best practices in community leadership

WCOM 313.Title: Writing Poetry
WCOM 313.Prerequisites: Prerequisites CCOM 200 or WCOM 203 or permission of the Centre
WCOM 313.Course_Description: Production of original works of literary poetry in English. Advanced study and application ofwriting techniques,craft elements, poetic approaches and formal considerations used in contemporary free verse. In-depth instruction in the nuanced use of sound, line, image, rhythm, figurative language, and form. Craft, analysis of modern and contemporary literary poems, workshop-style critique, multiple drafts, and substantive revision

WCOM 314.Title: Communicating Science
WCOM 314.Course_Description: Production of written and oral assignments (in English) designed to communicate scientific problems and findings to varied audiences Analysis of the disciplinary conventions of scientific discourse in terms of audience, purpose, organization, and style; comparative rhetorical analysis of academic and popular genres, including abstracts, lab reports, research papers, print and online journalism

WCOM 317.Title: Writing the Internet
WCOM 317.Course_Description: Critical assessment of digital genres in terms of audience, purpose, organization, and style; application of rhetorical strategies for effective communication in digital contexts in English. Topics and readings derived from writing pedagogy and critical analyses of online environments: technological affordances, non-linear structure, “living” texts, online identity, network dynamics, authorial collaboration

WCOM 323.Title: Writing Short Fiction
WCOM 323.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 323.Prerequisites: CCOM 200 or WCOM 203 or permission of the Centre
WCOM 323.Course_Description: Production of original works of literary short fiction in English. Advanced study and application of written storytelling techniques and craft elements used in contemporary short fiction forms, with a main focus on the short story. In-depth instruction in the nuanced creation of character, dialogue, scene, setting, point of view, narrative distance, and structure. Craft, analysis of published literary short fiction, workshopstyle critique, multiple drafts, and substantive revision

WCOM 333.Title: Writing Creative Nonfiction
WCOM 333.Prerequisites: CCOM 200 or WCOM 203 or permission of the Centre
WCOM 333.Course_Description: Production of original works of literary creative nonfiction in English. Advanced study and application of story telling techniques and craft elements used in forms such as the memoir essay, literary journalism, and the lyric essay. In-depth instruction in the nuanced use of structure, scene, narration, reflection, description, and researched information. Craft, analysis of published literary creative nonfiction essays, workshop-style critique, multiple drafts, and substantive revision

WCOM 363.Title: Plurilingual Writing
WCOM 363.Course_Description: Explores writing as a plurilingual practice through creative and academic compositions that draw on multiple linguistic resources. Examines how languages interact in meaning-making, narrative construction, and rhetorical expression. Focuses on translanguaging strategies, cross-linguistic genres, and plurilingual voice across diverse written forms

WCOM 371.Title: Selected Communication Topic 1
WCOM 371.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 371.Course_Description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication in English that is relevant to undergraduate students

WCOM 372.Title: Selected Communication Topic 2
WCOM 372.Course_Description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication in English that is relevant to undergraduate students

WCOM 414.Title: Advanced Communicating Science
WCOM 414.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 414.Prerequisites: CCOM 314 or WCOM 314 or permission of the Centre
WCOM 414.Course_Description: Use of digital platforms to produce written and oral assignments (in English) designed to communicate scientific challenges and findings to broad audiences. Rhetorical analysis of academic and popular genres including abstracts, researcher profiles, infographics, and serial and episodic podcasting

WCOM 417.Title: Digital Storytelling
WCOM 417.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 417.Prerequisites: CCOM 315 or WCOM 317, or permission of the Centre
WCOM 417.Course_Description: Analysis and application of digital storytelling strategiesthrough the production of long-form written and spokencontent for English-language audiences. Drafting,revision, concision, precision, and digital affordances inlong-form journalism, essays, and podcasts. Topicsinclude narrative structure, character development,accessibility, socio-technical analysis, and audioproduction

WCOM 550.Title: Business and Professional Communication
WCOM 550.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 550.Course_Description: Written and oral communication skills in English for business and professional purposes. Concepts and principles of effective written communication. Planning, composing, editing, and polishing documents of various lengths and formats; conventions of workplace correspondence; direct and indirect approaches to workplace messages; composing routine, persuasive, positive, and negative messages; planning and delivering effective presentations, including creating effective visuals

WCOM 555.Title: ESL: Business and Professional Communication
WCOM 555.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 555.Course_Description: Written and oral communication skills for business and professional purposes for students whose first language is not English. Concepts and principles of effective written communication. Planning, composing, editing, and polishing documents of various lengths and formats; conventions of workplace correspondence; direct and indirect approaches to workplace messages; composing routine, persuasive, positive, and negative messages; planning and delivering effective presentations, including creating effective visuals; strategies to address common English as Second Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax, and vocabulary

WCOM 624.Title: Communicating Research to the Public
WCOM 624.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 624.Course_Description: Production of written assignments designed to communicate complex ideas and research problems and findings to varied audiences in English. Analysis of discursive academic and policy conventions in terms of audience, purpose, organization, and style for their translation to non-specialist audiences, including the general public and/or policymakers

WCOM 627.Title: Communicating Research to the Digital Public
WCOM 627.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 627.Course_Description: Production of written and oral assignments designed to communicate complex ideas and research findings through digital platforms in English. Creation of projects that may include lay audience abstracts, content creation on social media, and the production of infographics, and podcasts

WCOM 635.Title: ESL: Strategies for Academic Communication
WCOM 635.Course_Description: Key language learning strategies for expressing complex ideas in academic writing across the disciplines. Corpus tools to identify collocations; strategies to build productive scholarly vocabulary; self-editing techniques to avoid common English-as-Second-Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax and mechanics

WCOM 642.Title: Cornerstones of Academic Writing
WCOM 642.Course_Description: Key strategies for scholarly communication across disciplines: reading scholarly texts for structure; applying these structures in writing assignments. Four cornerstones of academic writing: audience, purpose, organization, and style. Identifying and targeting audiences, clarifying the purposes served by different writing projects, organizing ideas, and developing mastery of rhetorical and stylistic conventions

WCOM 645.Title: ESL: Fundamentals of Academic Writing
WCOM 645.Course_Description: Key strategies for academic writing across disciplines: reading scholarly texts for structure; applying these structures in writing assignments; developing vocabulary building strategies; identifying and practicing nuances of scholarly English syntax. Self-editing techniques to avoid common English-as-Second-Language (ESL) errors; review of English grammar and mechanics

WCOM 652.Title: Fundamentals of Academic Presentations
WCOM 652.Course_Description: Developing and delivering academic presentations, with emphasis on how to structure content, critically evaluate content, and use rhetorical devices to enhance clarity

WCOM 655.Title: ESL: Pronunciation for Effective Communication
WCOM 655.Course_Description: Pronunciation skills for effective communication in English about research and complex ideas in academic settings with emphasis on features of pronunciation that most affect intelligibility

WCOM 661.Title: Literature Review 1: Summary and Critique
WCOM 661.Course_Description: Responsible and effective engagement with other scholars’ work in order to summarize and critique research literature. Focus on economic use of language and techniques for mobilizing existing scholarship in service of an original research project

WCOM 662.Title: Literature Review 2: Establishing Scholarly Niches
WCOM 662.Course_Description: Situating original student research in existing scholarship through analysis of literature in a discipline; application of techniques for framing contributions

WCOM 671.Title: Selected Topics in Communication 1
WCOM 671.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 671.Course_Description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication relevant to postgraduates. The content can vary from year to year and will be announced prior to registration

WCOM 672.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.

WCOM 676.Title: Thesis Writing Lab
WCOM 676.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 676.Course_Description: Writing and revising of a chapter or manuscript for structure, clarity, cohesion, and disciplinary conventions; practical strategies for writing and rewriting productively; techniques for organizing ideas and editing for flow; peer review

WCOM 690.Title: Writing for Graduate Students
WCOM 690.Course_Description: Audience, purpose, organization, and style of graduate-level academic writing with attention to mechanics, textual analysis, critical thinking and editing skills. Common rhetorical patterns to organize research writing, including problem-solution, general-specific, process description, data commentary, article summary/critique

WCOM 695.Title: ESL: Academic Writing for Graduate Students
WCOM 695.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WCOM 695.Course_Description: Structuring an academic paper and expressing complex ideas in English using common rhetorical patterns. Academic reading, critical thinking, vocabulary building, and writing mechanics. Self-editing to enhance cohesion and avoid common English-as-a-Second Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax, and vocabulary

WILD 302.Title: Fish Ecology
WILD 302.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 302.Course_Description: Introduction to the biology and ecology of freshwater and marine fishes. Topics include taxonomy, physiology, biogeography, competition, predation, fishing, and conservation. Lab exercises and field trips emphasize familiarity with local fishes and their ecological interactions

WILD 307.Title: Natural History of Vertebrates
WILD 307.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 307.Course_Description: The diversity and natural history of Canadian vertebrates illustrated with trophic, phylogenetic, and macroecological approaches

WILD 350.Title: Mammalogy
WILD 350.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 350.Course_Description: This course focuses on the evolution, classification, ecology and behaviour of mammals and relations between humans and mammals. Also structure, systematics and identification of local and world mammals, as well as field methods will be emphasized

WILD 375.Title: Issues: Environmental Sciences
WILD 375.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 375.Course_Description: Principles and trends in global ecology as they pertain to agricultural and natural ecosystems and the impact of environmental change on food production

WILD 401.Title: Fisheries and Wildlife Management
WILD 401.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 401.Prerequisites: WILD 307 and ENVB 305 or permission of the instructor
WILD 401.Course_Description: Principles of fisheries and wildlife management are considered and current practices of research and management are discussed

WILD 420.Title: Ornithology
WILD 420.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 420.Course_Description: Taxonomic relationships and evolution of birds. Examination of the physiology, migration, identification and ecological processes of North American birds

WILD 421.Title: Wildlife Conservation
WILD 421.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 421.Course_Description: Study of current controversial issues focusing on wildlife conservation. Topics include: animal rights, exotic species, ecotourism, urban wildlife, multi-use of national parks, harvesting of wildlife, biological controls, and endangered species

WILD 475.Title: Desert Ecology
WILD 475.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WILD 475.Terms_Offered: This course is not offered this catalogue year.
WILD 475.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s):Permission of the instructors is required to register. To be eligible students are required to have at least one systems-focused course, one ecology course and two organismal courses. Students should consult the instructors for list of appropriate courses
WILD 475.Course_Description: A three week field course exploring relationships between climate, geology, landforms, biodiversity, biotic adaptations and ecosystem conditions in the arid regions of Arizona and southern California. Focus is on the Sonoran and Mojave deserts but includes the transitions to adjacent grassland and forest biomes of the Sky Islands and Colorado Plateau. Exploration of issues arising from human use of land and water, and conservation in arid environments. Experiential learning involving team and individual projects and assignments before and during the field trip

WMST 601.Title: Feminist Theories and Methods
WMST 601.Faculty: Inst for Gender, Sex & Fem St (Graduate Studies)
WMST 601.Course_Description: Examination of feminist theories and research methods from a variety of disciplinary perspectives

WOOD 441.Title: Integrated Forest Management
WOOD 441.Faculty: Natural Resource Sciences (Faculty of Agric Environ Sci)
WOOD 441.Prerequisites: Prerequisite(s): ENVB 210 or ENVB 222 or ENVR 202, or permission of instructor
WOOD 441.Course_Description: The study of silviculture and silvics and their application to forest management to sustain the production of wood and other ecological goods and services such as wildlife, water and landscape in natural forests and rural environments (agroforestry).
